# Lua API reference

<!-- Generated by tools/apidoc.lua from the source's comments: do not edit. -->

Every public function of the `paw` modules, with what its comment in the
source says, module by module; [Scripting](scripting.md) and
[Extensions](extensions.md) say how they fit together. The kernel's own
functions (`paw.api`, plain data in and out) are listed at the end.
`runtime/types/paw.lua` holds the same for editors (LuaLS).

## Module paw

- `paw.add_track(opts)`: A new track, last unless `opts.index` says where: `opts` as `paw.api.track_add` takes them (`name`, `volume`, `output` as a track or an id, ...).
- `paw.bounce(track, opts)`: Render a track with its devices to audio, as one clip on a new track right below it that feeds where it fed, and mute the original. Goes through `paw.render`, so `render.before` is heard. `opts.name` names the new track ("<name> (bounced)" by default), `opts.tail` is the seconds rendered after its last clip (2). Returns the new track, or nil when the track has no clips.
- `paw.buftype(name, def)`: Make a buffer type. See docs/scripting.md.

  ```lua
  paw.buftype("notes", { create = function(target) return {} end, render = function(win, canvas, ctx) end })
  ```

  Fields: `create(target, buf)` gives the buffer's state; `render(win, canvas, ctx)` draws (`ctx.buf` is the buffer, `win.state` the window's own); `on_key(win, key)` for keys with no mapping; `on_mouse(win, event)`; `title(buf)`; `bufname(target, buf)`; `options` (the buffer's to start with); `listed` (false keeps its buffers off `:ls`, and forgets each once no window shows it); `delete(buf)`; `time` (see `timebind`); `claims(name)`, whether a name is a target of the type's by its form (`:vs paw://lane/3`); `window()`, the window to draw when none in the tabs shows the type (one in a graphical frontend's window of its own). Key mappings for its windows are mapped with `{ view = name }`.  Everything a view can do, per window: `grid(win)` (the cursor the keymap moves, as a view's `grid`), `describe(win)` (what `K` says), `status(win, ctx)` (the status line's `view` component), `subscope(win)`, `paint(win, g, ctx)` and `pointer(win, e)` (pixels in a graphical frontend), `help`, and what `paw.layout.powers` maps: `keymaps`, `motions`, `textobjects`, `operators`, whose functions get `ctx.win` and `ctx.buf`.
- `paw.cancel`: the same as `paw.api.timer_stop`.
- `paw.clip(id)`: The clip of an id, as a `paw.Clip`.
- `paw.cmd(name, args, ctx)`: Run a command. `args` is a table of arguments; `ctx` adds fields such as `count`.
- `paw.defer(fn, ms)`: Run `fn` once, after `ms` milliseconds (or as soon as the current turn ends).
- `paw.device(id)`: The device, clip or automation lane of an id, as an object.
- `paw.device_types()`: Descriptions of every kind of device that can be added to a track; one an extension added (`paw.plugins.add_dir`) says which, as `from`.
- `paw.emit(name, payload)`: Call every handler for `name`. A failing handler is reported and skipped. Returns true, or false and the reason when a handler returned `false, reason`: how a handler refuses what an event asks about (`edit.before`, `project.saving`, `key.pre`).
- `paw.every(ms, fn)`: Run `fn` every `ms` milliseconds. Returns a handle for `paw.cancel`.
- `paw.flush()`: Deliver the change events for edits made so far. The kernel does this at the end of every turn; call `paw.flush()` to have handlers run sooner.
- `paw.import_audio(path, opts)`: Bring a sound file into the project: on a new track named after the file (or on `opts.track`), at the cursor (or `opts.start`). Returns the clip.
- `paw.inspect(value, indent, seen)`: Render any value as readable Lua-like text.
- `paw.is_audio_file(path)`: Whether a path names a sound file, by its ending.
- `paw.lane(id)`: The automation lane of an id, as a `paw.Lane`.
- `paw.notify(text, level)`: Show a message. `level` is "info" (default), "warn" or "error".
- `paw.off(id)`: Stop listening: `id` is what `paw.on` or `paw.once` returned.
- `paw.on(pattern, fn, opts)`: Listen for an event. Returns a handle for `paw.off`.
- `paw.once(pattern, fn)`: Listen for an event once: the handler is removed after its first call.
- `paw.open(path, opts)`: Open what a path names: a sound file as a new track, anything else as a project, with plugins offline as `opts` says (see `paw.loading.open`).
- `paw.redo`: the same as `paw.api.redo`.
- `paw.render(path, opts)`: Render the project to a file, and render stems: see `paw/render.lua` for the options. `paw.render_status()` and `paw.render_cancel()` look after a render running in the background; `paw.render_ranges` holds the named ranges a render can take.
- `paw.render_cancel()`: Stop the render running in the background.
- `paw.render_status()`: The render running in the background (`{ path, fraction, seconds }`), or nil.
- `paw.render_stems(dir, opts)`: Render each track to a file of its own in `dir` (see `paw/render.lua` for `opts`).
- `paw.render_tags(set)`: The tags of the project's rendered files: `paw.render_tags()`, `paw.render_tags({ artist = "Me" })`.
- `paw.restore_clip(snap, track)`: Add a clip from a snapshot to a track.
- `paw.restore_device(snap, track, index)`: Add a device from a snapshot to a track, at the end of the chain or at the 1-based `index`.
- `paw.restore_track(snap, index)`: Make a track from a snapshot, at a 1-based position in the track list.
- `paw.track(which)`: A track by id, or by name.
- `paw.tracks()`: Every track, in order, as `paw.Track` objects (the master is `paw.master`).
- `paw.try(fn, ...)`: Call a function, reporting an error as a message instead of raising it. Returns true and the function's results, or false and the error.
- `paw.undo`: the same as `paw.api.undo`.
- `paw.wait`: the same as `paw.api.wait`.

## Module paw.Clip

- `paw.Clip:add_note(note)`

  ```lua
  clip:add_note({ pitch = "E4", start = 1, length = 0.5, velocity = 90 })
  clip:add_note({ pitch = "G4", start = 2, attr = paw.attr.m2("11.A") })   -- pizzicato
  ```

  Returns the note's place among the clip's notes.
- `paw.Clip:add_notes(notes)`: Add several notes as one edit (as `add_note` takes each).
- `paw.Clip:controls()`: What the clip does besides notes: controller moves, the pitch wheel, pressure and program changes, each `{ start, type, value }` with `start` in beats from the start of the clip. `type` is "cc" (with `number`), "bend" (-1 to 1), "pressure", "registered" or "assignable" (with `bank` and `index`), or "program" (with `program` and maybe `bank`); values run from 0 to 1 at any resolution. With `key` a move belongs to the note on that key alone, as in MIDI 2.0: its own bend, pressure or controller.
- `paw.Clip:duplicate(opts)`: Copy the clip. By default the copy goes right after the original.
- `paw.Clip:edit_notes(edit)`: Change, remove and add several notes as one edit. Every index is a note's place before the call:

  ```lua
  clip:edit_notes({ set = { { index = 3, start = 1 } }, remove = { 5, 6 }, add = { note } })
  ```
- `paw.Clip:exists()`: Whether the clip is still in the project.
- `paw.Clip:get()`: Everything about the clip as plain data (`paw.api.clip_get`).
- `paw.Clip:note_at(pitch, beat)`: The note on a pitch sounding at a beat of the clip, and its place among the clip's notes; nothing when there is none.
- `paw.Clip:notes(range)`: The notes of a MIDI clip: a list of { pitch, start, length, velocity }, with `start` in beats from the start of the clip, `meta`, a table of extension data such as a lyric, on notes that have any, and `attr`, the MIDI 2.0 attribute of the note's start (`{ type, data }`, see `paw.attr`), on notes that have one.  With a range, only the notes sounding within it, and as a second value the place of each in the whole list, for `set_note` and `remove_note`:

  ```lua
  local notes, at = clip:notes({ from = 4, to = 8, low = "C3", high = "C5" })
  ```
- `paw.Clip:peaks(n)`: The waveform of an audio clip: `n` { min, max, rms } entries, each covering an equal part of what the clip plays, scaled by its gain: how far the wave reaches each way (-1 to 1) and how loud it is there. Cached, so drawing code can ask for it every frame.
- `paw.Clip:remove()`: Take the clip out of its track.
- `paw.Clip:remove_note(index)`: Remove the note at a place among the clip's notes (from 1).
- `paw.Clip:set_controls(controls)`

  ```lua
  clip:set_controls({ { start = 0, type = "cc", number = 64, value = 1 },
                      { start = 1, type = "bend", key = "E4", value = 0.02 } })
  ```
- `paw.Clip:set_note(index, fields)`: Change one note, named by its place among the clip's notes (from 1), without touching the others: `clip:set_note(3, { length = 2 })`. Returns the note's place afterwards, since notes stay in the order they start. `attr = false` takes its attribute away.
- `paw.Clip:set_notes(notes)`: Replace every note of the clip with `notes` (as `add_note` takes each).
- `paw.Clip:snapshot()`: The clip as plain data, for `paw.restore_clip`.
- `paw.Clip:track()`: The track the clip is on.

## Module paw.Device

- `paw.Device:automate(param)`: The lane for a parameter, made if there is none yet.

  ```lua
  synth:automate("cutoff"):add(0, 200)
  ```
- `paw.Device:close_editor()`: Close the plugin's own window.
- `paw.Device:exists()`: Whether the device is still in the project.
- `paw.Device:get()`: Everything about the device as plain data (`paw.api.device_get`).
- `paw.Device:info()`: The description of this device: its name, category, format, and its parameters with their ranges. A plugin's parameters are those of this instance, which is the only place they are known.
- `paw.Device:lane(param)`: The lane for a parameter, if there is one.
- `paw.Device:lanes()`: The automation lanes of the device's parameters, as `paw.Lane` objects.
- `paw.Device:move(index, track)`: Move within the chain, or to another track: `device:move(1)`, `device:move(2, other)`.
- `paw.Device:open_editor()`: Show the plugin's own window.
- `paw.Device:remove()`: Take the device off its track.
- `paw.Device:restart()`: Show the plugin's own window. `device.editor` is "open", "closed", or nil for devices that have none. Start the device again: for a plugin that stopped working (`stopped` says why) or never loaded. It comes back with the state the project last had of it.
- `paw.Device:set(name, value)`: Set one parameter, or several from a table.

  ```lua
  device:set("cutoff", 800)
  device:set({ cutoff = 800, resonance = 0.4 })
  ```
- `paw.Device:set_offline(on)`: Set the device offline: not made at all (no process for a plugin), passed over, its state and parameters kept as they are; or back online.
- `paw.Device:set_output(pair, track)`: Play the device's output pair `pair` (2 and on: the first plays on its own track) into a track, or nowhere with nil. `device.outputs` is a table of pair number to track id; `device.ports.outputs` names the pairs.
- `paw.Device:set_sidechain(track, opts)`: Listen to another track's sound as the device's side-chain: a compressor on the bass ducks under the kick with `comp:set_sidechain(kick)`. `{ pre = true }` takes it before that track's fader, pan and mute; nil (or no track) takes the side-chain away. `device.sidechain` is the track's id.
- `paw.Device:snapshot()`: The device as plain data, for `paw.restore_device`. A plugin is captured by its state, which holds more than its parameters do.
- `paw.Device:track()`: The track this device is on.
- `paw.Device:value_at(param, beat)`: What a parameter is at a beat while playing: the lane's value when one is on, else the device's own.

## Module paw.Lane

- `paw.Lane:add(beat, value)`: Add a point, replacing any at the same beat. The value is in the target's own units: dB for volume, -1 to 1 for pan, the parameter's range otherwise.
- `paw.Lane:clear()`: Remove every point of the lane.
- `paw.Lane:exists()`: Whether the lane is still in the project.
- `paw.Lane:get()`: Everything about the lane as plain data (`paw.api.lane_get`).
- `paw.Lane:points()`: The points as a list of { beat, value }, sorted by beat.
- `paw.Lane:remove()`: Take the lane away, and the automation in it.
- `paw.Lane:set_points(points)`: Replace the points: `lane:set_points({ { 0, -60 }, { 8, 0 } })`. Points may also be written { beat = 0, value = -60 }.
- `paw.Lane:track()`: The track the lane belongs to.
- `paw.Lane:value_at(beat)`: The value at a beat, whether or not the lane is on. Nil without points.

## Module paw.Track

- `paw.Track:add_clip(opts)`: Add a clip. With `file` it is an audio clip, otherwise a MIDI clip.

  ```lua
  track:add_clip({ start = 0, length = 4, notes = { { pitch = "C4", start = 0, length = 1 } } })
  track:add_clip({ start = 8, file = "take1.wav" })
  ```
- `paw.Track:add_device(kind, params, opts)`: Add a device to the end of the chain, or at the 1-based `opts.index`.

  ```lua
  track:add_device("synth", { cutoff = 800 })
  ```
- `paw.Track:automate(target)`: The lane for "volume" or "pan", made if there is none yet.

  ```lua
  track:automate("volume"):set_points({ { 0, -60 }, { 8, 0 } })
  ```
- `paw.Track:clip_at(beat)`: The clip covering `beat`, if any. The later clip wins where two overlap.
- `paw.Track:clips()`: The track's clips, as `paw.Clip` objects.
- `paw.Track:device(which)`: The first device of a kind, or the device at a 1-based position.
- `paw.Track:devices()`: The track's devices in the order they process, as `paw.Device` objects.
- `paw.Track:duplicate()`: Copy the track with its devices, clips and automation, placing the copy after it.
- `paw.Track:exists()`: Whether the track is still in the project.
- `paw.Track:get()`: A plain table with every field of the track, read once.
- `paw.Track:lane(target)`: The lane for "volume" or "pan", if there is one.
- `paw.Track:lanes()`: The automation lanes of the track, its devices' included.
- `paw.Track:meter()`: Peak level as linear `left, right`.
- `paw.Track:midi(event)`: Send a MIDI message to this track's devices now, outside the timeline: a controller, the pitch wheel, pressure, or with `key` one note's own.

  ```lua
  track:midi({ type = "cc", number = 1, value = 0.5 })
  track:midi({ type = "bend", value = -0.25 })
  track:midi({ type = "bend", key = "C4", value = 0.1 })
  ```
- `paw.Track:move(index)`: Move to a 1-based position in the track list.
- `paw.Track:note_off(pitch)`: Stop a note, or every note when `pitch` is left out.
- `paw.Track:note_on(pitch, velocity, attr)`: Start a note now, outside the timeline. `pitch` may be a name like "C4". With `attr`, a MIDI 2.0 attribute (`paw.attr`), the note carries it, and what the track's `attr_map` sends for it goes first.
- `paw.Track:play_note(pitch, velocity, ms, attr)`: Play a note for `ms` milliseconds (default 200), with `attr` if given.
- `paw.Track:remove()`: Take the track out of the project, with its clips and devices.
- `paw.Track:send(target, level, opts)`: Send some of this track's output to another track. `level` is in dB. With `{ pre = true }` the send is taken before the fader and pan, so it keeps its level when the fader moves: `vocal:send(reverb, -6, { pre = true })`.
- `paw.Track:snapshot()`: Everything about the track as plain data: its settings, devices (plugins with their state), clips and automation. `paw.restore_track` makes a track from it again, in this project or after the original is gone.
- `paw.Track:value_at(target, beat)`: What "volume" or "pan" is at a beat while playing: the lane's value when one is on, else the track's own.

## Module paw.address

- `paw.address.children(uri)`: What an address holds, one level down.
- `paw.address.clip(id)`: A clip's address.
- `paw.address.device(id)`: A device's address, under its track's.
- `paw.address.edit(changes, label)`: Carry out a workspace edit: every change is checked first, and nothing is done unless all can be; then all are made as one undo step labelled `label`. Returns true, or nil and why not.

  ```lua
  paw.address.edit({ { uri = "paw://track/3", set = { volume = -6 } },
                     { uri = "paw://clip/7/note/41", set = { pitch = 62 } } }, "Lower the bass")
  ```
- `paw.address.find_note(clip, id)`: The note of a clip with an id, and its place in the clip (from 1).
- `paw.address.lane(id)`: An automation lane's address.
- `paw.address.location(uri, selector)`: A location: an address and, optionally, a part of it.
- `paw.address.marker(id)`: A marker's address.
- `paw.address.matches(pattern, uri)`: Whether an address matches a pattern: `paw://track/*` (one level), `paw://track/**` (any depth), or an exact address.
- `paw.address.note(clip, id)`: A note's address: its clip, and the note's id there.
- `paw.address.of(object)`: The address of an object of the scripting interface (`paw.track(3)`, `paw.clip(7)`, a device) or of a table `paw.api` gave (with its fields).
- `paw.address.param(device, key)`: A device parameter's address, by its key.
- `paw.address.parent(uri)`: The address that holds this one (a note's clip, a device's track), or nil.
- `paw.address.parse(uri)`: An address in parts: `{ kind = "note", track?, device?, param?, send?, clip?, note?, lane?, marker?, control?, number?, path?, segments }`, or nil when it is not one. The fragment (`#mix`) is kept as `fragment`.
- `paw.address.project()`: The address of the project, the tempo map, a track, a clip, a note, a lane, a marker, a rendered file and a send, as `parse` reads them.
- `paw.address.render(path)`: A rendered file's address.
- `paw.address.resolve(uri)`: What an address names, as `paw.api` has it (a note also says its `place`; a parameter is `{ key, value, info }`), or nil when it is gone.
- `paw.address.scheme(name, spec)`: Add a kind of address: `paw://<name>/...`, for what an extension keeps (the vocal editor's phrases, a score's measures). `spec.resolve(uri, parts)` gives the thing or nil; optional `of(object)`, `children(uri, parts)`, `parent(uri, parts)`, `go(location, parts)` and `where(location, parts)` for the quickfix list (going there, and naming it in a few words), and `edit(change, parts)` to apply a workspace edit's change to it (which must make its edits through `paw.api`, so that they join the undo step).
- `paw.address.send(track, target)`: The address of a track's send to another.
- `paw.address.tempo()`: The tempo map's address.
- `paw.address.track(id)`: A track's address.
- `paw.address.track_of(uri)`: The track an address belongs to, if any.
- `paw.address.within(uri, ancestor)`: Whether `uri` is `ancestor` or lies inside it (a note inside its clip, a parameter inside its device and track). Everything is inside the project.

## Module paw.annotation

- `paw.annotation.get(uri, exact)`: The labels on an address exactly (`exact`), or on it and what it holds.
- `paw.annotation.reset(namespace, doc)`: Forget a namespace's labels, of one document or all; with no namespace, everyone's.
- `paw.annotation.set(namespace, doc, list)`: Publish what `namespace` labels in a document, replacing what it put there before.

## Module paw.attr

- `paw.attr.delay_of(track, attr)`: The milliseconds a note with `attr` (nil for none) on `track` plays early (below 0) or late by the track's `attr_map`, so that a library slow to speak still sounds on the beat; 0 without a map.
- `paw.attr.describe(attr)`: What an attribute is, for people: `{ code, tag, name, class, text }` (`code` and `class` only for articulations), where `tag` is a few letters for the piano roll and `text` one line for `K`. Nil for none.
- `paw.attr.m2(code, opts)`: An articulation's code as an attribute, or an attribute as its code (nil when it is not an articulation of M2-123). `opts` adds what a code leaves out: `variation` (0 to 15), `direction` ("down", "up", 1 or 2), `string` (1 to 7, highest first), `reset` (round robin).
- `paw.attr.parts(attr)`: The fields of an attribute's data, as M2-123 lays them out: `{ type, data, subclass, variation, direction, reset, string }`. Nil for none.
- `paw.attr.same(a, b)`: The same attribute: both none, or the same type and data.

## Module paw.audio

- `paw.audio.choices(track)`: Everything a track's input can be, in order, under three headings (`group`): "audio" (none, each channel of the input device, each pair of neighbouring channels), "midi" (every port, or one) and "channel" (every MIDI channel, or one). Each is `{ group, label, checked, value }`; give it to `M.choose`. A choice that is saved but not there now is listed too, marked as missing, so that it can be seen and changed.
- `paw.audio.choose(track, choice)`: Take a choice from `M.choices`. A MIDI port or channel is only heard on a track without audio input, so choosing one takes the audio input away.
- `paw.audio.choose_engine(choice)`: Take a choice from `M.engine_choices`.
- `paw.audio.device()`: The input device's short name, or nil when there is none.
- `paw.audio.devices`: the same as `paw.api.audio_devices`.
- `paw.audio.engine_choices()`: What can be chosen where the devices are: under the headings (`group`) "output", "input", "block", "rate" and "backend" (the sound system), each `{ group, label, checked, value }` for `M.choose_engine`, and `info` lines that cannot be chosen.
- `paw.audio.label(t)`: What a track takes in, in a few words: `UR22mkII · 1/2` for audio, `MIDI · Keystation · ch 1` for MIDI from one port. Nil for a track that takes nothing in particular: no audio, and MIDI from everywhere.
- `paw.audio.level(t, levels)`: The level of what arrives at a track's audio input, 0 to 1, whether or not the track is armed or monitored; 0 for a track without one.
- `paw.audio.levels`: the same as `paw.api.input_levels`.
- `paw.audio.load(cpu)`: How busy the engine is, 0 to 1, as the status line and every frontend show it: the load of its blocks averaged over about a second, given in steps of 2.5% and moved only when the average has left the step shown. A block's own load wavers all the time, the more so on a busy machine, and each change of it would be drawn again in the terminal and sent to every window, which then drew a frame for it. `cpu`: the load just read (`api.engine_get().cpu`), when the caller has it.
- `paw.audio.short(name)`: A device's name made short enough for a track header: the maker's name goes when a model number follows it, and so does a trailing number.

  ```lua
  "Steinberg UR22mkII 0" → "UR22mkII", "Bose NC 700 HP" → "Bose NC 700 HP"
  ```
- `paw.audio.summary()`: The engine in a few words, for the transport bar: `pipewire · UR22mkII · 48 kHz`.
- `paw.audio.timing()`: Sample rate, block size and latencies in one line.
- `paw.audio.use(opts)`: Open other devices: `output` and `input` by name or part of one (`"default"` for the system's), `buffer` in frames (0 for the device's own), `rate` in Hz (0 for the device's own), `backend` the sound system (`"auto"`, `"pipewire"`, `"alsa"`, `"jack"`). What is left out stays. The choice belongs to this machine and is remembered for the next run; a name that matches nothing is an error.

## Module paw.audition

- `paw.audition.builtin(track, at)`: A phrase for a track with nothing to play: a bar of a beat for a drum track; else the key's tonic chord held, then arpeggiated up and back, in the track's range. `{ notes, length, label }`.
- `paw.audition.file(path)`: Hear a sound file on its own, from its start, in place of whatever was.
- `paw.audition.has_instrument(track)`: Whether a track has an instrument to play notes with.
- `paw.audition.keep()`: Keep the trial's edits as one undo step.
- `paw.audition.midi_file(path, bars)`: Play the first `bars` bars of a MIDI file (2 when nil), at its own tempo, once: pitched parts through `player()`, its drums (channel 10) through a kit. Returns the label.
- `paw.audition.outline_lines(outline, width, rows, position, length)`: A sound file's outline as `rows` lines `width` columns wide, the loudest part of each column drawn up from the bottom, and the column the file has got to, if `position` (seconds of `length`) is given.
- `paw.audition.phrase(track, notes, opts)`: Play `notes` (`{ pitch, start, length, velocity }`, `start` in beats from the phrase's start; a note's own `track` over the phrase's) through a track, again every `opts.length` beats (or once with `loop = false`). `opts.label` says what it is; a phrase with the same `opts.key` as the one playing goes on without starting again, so that what changes is only the sound. `opts.tempo` is its own tempo, else the project's at `opts.at` (the cursor's). Nothing is played while the transport runs.
- `paw.audition.player(drums)`: A track to play notes through: the cursor's when it has an instrument, else one added as a trial (with the built-in synth, or drums) that `revert` takes away. `drums` asks for a drum kit.
- `paw.audition.quiet()`: Stop what is heard (phrase and file), leaving a trial as it is.
- `paw.audition.revert()`: Put the project back as it was before the trial, if there is one.
- `paw.audition.state()`: What is heard now: `{ kind = "phrase", label, track, notes, length, silent }`, `{ kind = "file", file, state, position, length, outline }` or nil; `trial` is true while a trial's edits stand.
- `paw.audition.stop()`: Stop what is heard and take a trial back.
- `paw.audition.through(track)`: Play what a track plays around the cursor through it, over and over (`track_phrase`), so that a sound tried on it is heard with its own notes; the loop goes on while only the sound changes. Returns what is heard, in words.
- `paw.audition.track_phrase(track)`: What a track plays around the cursor, as a phrase: the bar of its MIDI clip at the cursor, else the last bar before the cursor that has notes, else the first that has any; `builtin` when it has none. `{ notes, length, label, at }`.
- `paw.audition.try(fn)`: Make the edits `fn` makes as a trial, in place of the last one: they are heard and seen, and `revert` takes them back without a trace. Returns what `fn` returns; an error takes the edits back and is raised.

## Module paw.autosave

- `paw.autosave.alternatives(path)`: What can stand in for the project file `path` when it cannot be opened: its `.bak` (the file as it was before the last save) and the newest safety copy of it, newest first: { file, path, kind, time }.
- `paw.autosave.choices()`: Everything `:recover` offers: the stand-ins for a project that would not open, then the copies left by sessions that ended badly.
- `paw.autosave.copy(force)`: Write a copy now, if the project has changed since the last one (or `force`, as when a take begins). Returns the file written, or nil.
- `paw.autosave.file()`: The file this session's copy of the project goes in: one per project file, or per session for a project that has no file yet.
- `paw.autosave.import_take(file)`: Bring an orphaned take in: on the track it was recorded for, if one has the name it starts with, or on a new one, at the start of the song.
- `paw.autosave.left_behind()`: The copies left by sessions that are gone: { file, path, name, time }.
- `paw.autosave.offer(path, err)`: Offer the alternatives to a project that would not open, if there are any: `:recover` lists them first. Returns how many there are.
- `paw.autosave.orphan_takes()`: Recorded takes in the project's `media` directory that no clip refers to and that were written after the project was last saved: what a session that ended during or after a take, without saving, leaves. (A take that was undone before a save is not one.) { file, name }.
- `paw.autosave.recover(file, opts)`: Open a copy that was left behind, as the project it was a copy of. `opts.as_path` opens it under that file name instead (a `.bak`, which is kept); `opts.plugins_offline` opens it with every plugin offline, in case one of them is what ended the session.

## Module paw.canvas

- `paw.canvas.back(name)`: Give the keyboard back to the main window from a view in a window of its own: to the window that had it before the view went there, else the arrange view.
- `paw.canvas.cell_event(window, event, bare)`: A pointer event in pixels as the terminal gives it to a view's `on_mouse`: in cells, `kind` down, up, drag or scroll_up and so on, `button`, and `mods` ("C", "A", "S"). Nil for what the terminal has no word for (the second click of a double one comes as down and up).
- `paw.canvas.close(name)`: Close a view's window of its own; the keyboard goes back to the main window, where it was before. A view docked in the layout instead closes its window there, as `:close` would.
- `paw.canvas.dock(name)`: Put a view in a window of its own back into the layout, with the keyboard: where it was before it popped out, else where it docks, else in a window split from the current one. What closing its window of its own does; `Ctrl-w d` in it does the same.
- `paw.canvas.draw(draw, px)`: The operations a function draws on a painter of `px.w` by `px.h` pixels: what a strip shows (`buf:strip`). `draw(g, px)` is given the painter and `px` itself; a failure is shown where it would have drawn.

  ```lua
  local ops = paw.canvas.draw(function(g, px) g:rect(0, 0, px.w, 2, { fill = "#ffffff" }) end, { w = 80, h = 40 })
  ```
- `paw.canvas.focus(name)`: Give a view in a window the keyboard, as a click in it does.
- `paw.canvas.glyph_outline(font, codepoint)`: A music font's glyph as commands and numbers in staff spaces from its origin, y down, from the fonts built into the kernel, or nil.
- `paw.canvas.key(name, keys)`: Keys typed in a view's window: they go to the key mappings with that view focused (or to a prompt that is open), as typed in the terminal. A view may give keys a meaning of its own in its window, as other programs do (`view.window_keys`, such as Ctrl-A for choosing every note), where the terminal keeps the one rule of every view.
- `paw.canvas.leave(name)`: A view about to show in a window of its own leaves the layout, so as not to show twice: its windows in the tabs close, keeping their place. Returns the window that had the keyboard, to give it back to. A view a frontend draws itself (the arrange view, the mixer...) stays where it is as well: the window of its own is a second look at it.
- `paw.canvas.open(name, opts)`: Show a view that paints in a graphical frontend and give it the keyboard: docked, as the terminal shows it, when it has a place in the layout (`paw.ui.dock`, or a window showing it); else, or with `window = true`, in a window of its own. A view already in a window of its own stays there. `opts`: `title`, `width`, `height` (what a window starts at), `window`.
- `paw.canvas.open_view(name, opts)`: Show any view in a window of a graphical frontend (the focused one when `name` is nil), and give it the keyboard. A view that paints is painted (`M.open`); any other is drawn as the terminal draws it, in cells of the window's monospace font, at whatever size the window has, with a line under it for prompts, messages and its keys. A view floating over the terminal's views moves into the window. `opts`: `title`, `width`, `height` (in pixels).

  ```lua
  paw.canvas.open_view("undotree")
  ```
- `paw.canvas.openable()`: The views a frontend can offer to open in a window: those that take the keyboard, `{ name, title }` each, by title. A view keeps itself off the list with `window = false`. A view with a painted twin (`painted = "name"` of a view that has `paint`) is offered as that one.
- `paw.canvas.paint(name, width, height, opts)`: Paint a view at a size. Returns the drawing as a list of operations:

  ```lua
  { "r", x, y, w, h, fill, stroke, stroke width, radius }
  { "t", x, y, text, colour, size, bold (0 or 1), align, width }
  { "p", path commands, stroke, stroke width, fill }
  { "m", x, y, w, h, text, colour, background, attributes }
  { "g", x, y, size, codepoint, colour, font }   a music font's glyph
  { "cut", x, y0, y1 }                           where a slice may end
  { "layer", name }                              what follows is that layer
  ```

  (attributes add up 1 bold, 4 italic, 8 underline, 32 strike), and the window's title, which a view may change as it goes. `opts`: `cell`, the size `{ w, h }` of a cell of the window's monospace font (or of the terminal's, for a surface), `fresh` when the window has nothing yet, `glyphs` when the frontend draws glyph ops itself (else they come as paths, and the markers are left out), `surface` when the drawing goes into a terminal's cells (the view leaves out what the terminal's own bars show, and its background), `colors` `{ fg, bg }`, the terminal's, and `bars` from a frontend that shows a view in a window of its own, out of sight of its main window's bottom: the status line and the command line are drawn under the view there. The view's `paint` is given these in its context, as `cell`, `surface`, `fg` and `bg`. A view that draws cells answers `{ same = true }` when nothing would change.
- `paw.canvas.paint_cells(name, window, width, height, opts)`: A view that draws cells, at a size in pixels: its snapshot (`paw.api.ui_view_snapshot`) as runs of text, a run of one style each. Drawn again only when a redraw has been asked for since, once a second for what changes on its own (times), and on every call while playing; `{ same = true }` when what it would draw is what it drew last. `window` keeps what was drawn. The view in a window of its own has a line under it for prompts, messages and the view's keys, unless the frontend draws a status line there itself (`opts.status`). A graphical frontend is sent its windows as scenes instead (`paw.ui.render_scene`).
- `paw.canvas.pointer(name, event)`: Pass a pointer event from a frontend to a view, which then has the keyboard: to its `pointer` in pixels, or for a view in cells to its `on_mouse` as the terminal would.
- `paw.canvas.shown(name)`: Whether a graphical frontend shows a view: in a window of its own, or docked where the seat's screen is a frontend's main area (one that has said its size to `paw.panes`, or the instance's own with no terminal).
- `paw.canvas.windows()`: The windows that are open, for a frontend: `{ name, title, width, height, cells }` each, `cells` for a view drawn as the terminal draws it.

## Module paw.commands

- `paw.commands.alias(alias, target)`: Make `alias` another name for `target`.
- `paw.commands.complete(line)`: What could finish a command line: a list of `{ text, label, desc }` with `text` the whole line it would become and `label` the part shown.

  ```lua
  paw.commands.complete("track.co")   --> { { text = "track.color", label = "track.color", desc = ... } }
  ```
- `paw.commands.define(name, run, opts)`: Define or replace a command.

  ```lua
  paw.command("track.mute", function(ctx) ... end, { desc = "Mute the track" })
  ```

  The handler receives `ctx` with `ctx.args` (positional and named arguments) and `ctx.count` (the number typed before a key mapping, or nil). With `opts.raw` the command line passes its text unsplit as `ctx.args[1]`. With `opts.range` it takes a range of bars in front (`:5,8name`) as `ctx.range`; see Ranges below.
- `paw.commands.exec(line, ctx)`: Run a command line, as typed after `:`, with a range in front if it has one.
- `paw.commands.get(name)`: The command of a name: `{ name, run, desc, ... }` as `paw.command` made it, or nil.
- `paw.commands.label(spec)`: What an undo step made by a command is called: its `label`, or the start of its description, before any example or alternative.
- `paw.commands.list()`: Every command, sorted by name.
- `paw.commands.main(name)`: What a bare extension name (`:notation`) stands for: its `.open` or `.show` command, where it has one.
- `paw.commands.owner()`: The extension being loaded, whose commands and keys these are: what `:help` takes them to.
- `paw.commands.parse(line)`: Split a command line into a name and arguments:

  ```lua
  `track.add Bass volume=-6` -> "track.add", { "Bass", volume = -6 }
  ```

  Quotes keep spaces together: `track.add "Lead Guitar"`, `name="Lead Guitar"`.
- `paw.commands.put(name, spec)`: Put a command back as `spec` (one `get` or `list` gave), or remove it with nil: what unloading an extension does with the commands it made.
- `paw.commands.range(line)`: Split a range off the front of a command line: the range, and the rest. Nil for the range when there is none; an error message instead of the rest when the range names nothing.
- `paw.commands.run`: the same as `paw.cmd`.
- `paw.commands.unknown(name)`: What to say about a name that is no command: the commands that start with it, if there are any.
- `paw.commands.used(name)`: Count a use of a command that was chosen by name (typed, or picked), so that pickers can put what is used often first. Kept in `paw.state`.
- `paw.commands.uses(name)`: How many times `used` has counted a command.

## Module paw.complete

- `paw.complete.accept(next_only)`: Write the alternative that shows into the clip, as one edit: all of it, or with `next_only` the notes of its first onset alone (a note, or the notes of a chord that start together), keeping the rest showing. The cursor goes to where the accepted part ends. Returns whether anything was written.
- `paw.complete.audition()`: Play the alternative that shows through the clip's track, starting a bar before it with the notes already there, without changing the project. Not while the transport runs.
- `paw.complete.cancel()`: Drop the request being answered, telling the sources that still owe an answer.
- `paw.complete.context(trigger)`: What a request is about: the clip open in the piano roll, where the suggestion starts and what is chosen there. Nil without an open clip.

  ```lua
  clip, track      ids
  start, length    where the clip is in the project, in beats
  at, pitch        where the suggestion starts (clip beats) and the cursor's pitch
  notes            the clip's notes, as `clip:notes()` gives them
  selection        the chosen notes, or nil
  grid, view, trigger ("manual" or "auto"), id
  key              `paw.harmony.key(at)` when there is such a module
  ```
- `paw.complete.current()`: What shows: `{ items, index, item, clip }`, or nil. A suggestion asked for by itself does not show while the transport plays or records.
- `paw.complete.dismiss()`: Hide what shows, and drop the request being answered.
- `paw.complete.list()`: The sources, highest priority first.
- `paw.complete.pending()`: Whether a request is waiting for answers.
- `paw.complete.poke()`: Start the idle pause again: after an edit.
- `paw.complete.register(spec)`: Add a source, or replace the one of the same name.
- `paw.complete.request(trigger)`: Ask every source for this view at once. `trigger` is "manual" (a key, the default) or "auto". Returns the request's id, or nil when there is nothing to ask about or nobody to ask.
- `paw.complete.select(n, absolute)`: Show the next alternative (`n` 1), the previous (-1), or with `absolute` the `n`th.
- `paw.complete.show(items, opts)`: Show items as ghost notes in the piano roll without being a source: a snippet's preview, what a fix would do. `opts.clip` is the clip they are for (the one open), `opts.keys = false` shows them only, without the keys that accept or step through them. Nothing, or an empty list, hides them.
- `paw.complete.tool()`: What the window's piano roll toolbar shows of completion: nil without sources.
- `paw.complete.unregister(name)`: Remove the source of a name.

## Module paw.controls

- `paw.controls.add(clip, start, kind, number)`: Add a move at `start` beats into the clip: of `kind` ("cc" with `number`, "bend", "pressure", "program"), at rest or 0. Returns it.
- `paw.controls.cells(clip, row)`: The text of each column of a row, by the names in `M.columns`.
- `paw.controls.chosen(clip)`: The places of the chosen moves of `clip`, in order.
- `paw.controls.clear(clip)`: Choose none of the clip's controller moves.
- `paw.controls.edit(clip, row, column, text)`: Change one cell of a row from text written as the list shows it. Errors say what is wrong.
- `paw.controls.fraction(kind, value)`: A move's value as a height in the strip, and a height as a value.
- `paw.controls.is(control, kind, number)`: Whether a move is of the strip's kind.
- `paw.controls.line(clip, kind, number, beat0, f0, beat1, f1, free)`: Draw a straight line of moves of the strip's kind from `beat0` at height `f0` to `beat1` at `f1`: it replaces the moves of that kind between, one to each step of the grid (each 32nd of a beat when `free`), both ends included. The new moves are then the chosen ones.
- `paw.controls.move(clip, dbeat, dfraction, free)`: Move the chosen moves `dbeat` later and `dfraction` of the strip's height up. The first of them lands on the grid unless `free`; the rest keep their distance from it, and none leaves the clip or the strip.
- `paw.controls.remove(clip)`: Take the chosen moves away. Returns how many went.
- `paw.controls.remove_row(clip, row)`: Take a row away.
- `paw.controls.rows(clip)`: Every note and move of a clip, in time order, as rows of the list: a note `{ kind = "note", place, start, note }`, a move `{ kind = "control", place, start, control }`. Notes come before moves at the same time. Notes and moves hidden by a trim of the clip's edges are left out.
- `paw.controls.select(clip, place, mode)`: Choose one move by its place: `mode` "only", "add" or "toggle".
- `paw.controls.select_box(clip, kind, number, beat0, low, beat1, high, mode)`: Choose the moves of the strip's kind that a box touches: from `beat0` to `beat1` and from height `low` to `high`, in any order. `mode` as for `select`. Returns how many are chosen.
- `paw.controls.value(kind, fraction)`: A height in the strip, from 0 to 1, as a move's value.

## Module paw.cursor

- `paw.cursor.clip()`: The clip under the cursor, if any.
- `paw.cursor.index()`: 1-based position of the cursor track in the track list.
- `paw.cursor.lane_id()`: The automation lane row the cursor is on: a lane of the cursor track shown as a row (see `paw.lanes`), or nil when it is on the track itself.
- `paw.cursor.line()`: 1-based row of the cursor among every row drawn, lanes included.
- `paw.cursor.move_track(delta)`: Move by rows. In normal mode the rows of open automation lanes count; after an operator or in a selection only tracks do, as for `dj`.
- `paw.cursor.row()`: 1-based row of the cursor track among the tracks that are drawn: the same as `index` until a group is folded.
- `paw.cursor.set_beat(beat)`: Put the cursor at a beat (not before 0).
- `paw.cursor.set_track(track, lane)`: Put the cursor on a track, or with `lane` on one of its lane rows.
- `paw.cursor.snap(beat)`: Round a position to the arrange grid.
- `paw.cursor.track()`: The track the cursor is on, as a `paw.Track`, or nil.
- `paw.cursor.track_id()`: Id of the track the cursor is on, falling back to the first track when that track is gone. Nil when the project has no tracks.

## Module paw.curves

- `paw.curves.copy(q)`: A copy of a point.
- `paw.curves.ease(shape, t, tension)`: Where a stretch is `t` of the way from one point to the next, 0 to 1, as the model plays it (crates/paw-core/src/model.rs, `smooth`).
- `paw.curves.fit(t, points)`: Points made fit for a curve: sorted, and every stretch of a shape it does not have written out as short pieces of one it has.
- `paw.curves.generate(wave, from, to, opts)`: A wave from beat `from` to beat `to`: `opts.rate` beats a cycle, `opts.depth` of the height, about `opts.centre` (a fraction, 0.5 when left out), turned into values with `opts.unfrac`. `opts.seed` makes a random one the same each time. Smooth shapes where `opts.smooth` (the curve has them), else many points.
- `paw.curves.is_curve(uri)`: Whether a text names a curve: an address `target` can read.
- `paw.curves.provide(name, fn)`: Make curves of addresses of your own: `fn(uri, parts)` returns a target with `points`, `write`, `name`, `format`, `lo`, `hi` and the rest, or nil to leave the address to the others (docs/scripting.md, Curves).
- `paw.curves.quantize(points, grid)`: Points moved onto the grid; of two that land on one step the later stays.
- `paw.curves.smooth(points, times)`: Softer moves: each value the mean of its own and its neighbours', `times` over. The first and the last stay where they are.
- `paw.curves.sorted(points)`: Points sorted by beat, those at the same beat kept in the order given.
- `paw.curves.splice(points, from, to, new)`: Replace the points from beat `from` to beat `to` (both included) with `new`, keeping the rest: what drawing over a stretch does.
- `paw.curves.target(uri)`: The curve at an address, or nil and why not.
- `paw.curves.thin(points, tolerance, frac)`: Fewer points for the same curve: a point goes when the curve without it strays from it by less than `tolerance` (a fraction of the drawing's height, through `frac`). Points that hold or ease stay.
- `paw.curves.value_at(points, beat)`: The value of a point list at a beat: the nearest point's before the first and after the last, nil with no points.

## Module paw.curves.editor

- `paw.curves.editor.add(on_curve)`: Add a point at the cursor: at the cursor's value, or with `on_curve` at the curve's value there.
- `paw.curves.editor.automate(device_id, key)`: Automate a device's parameter: make its lane with a first point at the value it has, at the arrange cursor's beat, show the track's lanes as rows with the cursor on the new one, and say so.
- `paw.curves.editor.climb(n)`: Move the cursor's value `n` steps up.
- `paw.curves.editor.current()`: The curve window the keyboard is in: the current window, or the one a graphical frontend shows.
- `paw.curves.editor.cycle_shape()`: The next shape for the stretch from the point under the cursor.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_finish()`: Keep the wave as it is.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_next(by)`: Choose the next shape (`by` 1) or the one before (-1) while generating.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_step(by)`: Step the current choice of the wave under way, or go to the next choice.
- `paw.curves.editor.gen_text()`: What the wave under way reads as on the bottom line.
- `paw.curves.editor.generate(wave, from, to, opts)`: Make a wave over a stretch of the curve, from beat `from` to `to`: `wave` by name or number in `paw.curves.waves`; `opts.rate` and `opts.depth` as numbers or places in their lists. The choices can then be stepped through until `<C-y>` or `<Esc>` keeps them.
- `paw.curves.editor.grid(factor)`: Make the editor's grid `factor` times as fine or as coarse.
- `paw.curves.editor.insert_finish()`: Write what was drawn, as one undo step.
- `paw.curves.editor.insert_mark()`: Put the cursor's beat and value among the points drawn.
- `paw.curves.editor.insert_start(on_curve)`: Start drawing at the cursor: from here, each move of the cursor puts a point where it lands, at its value. Nothing is written until insert mode is left.
- `paw.curves.editor.move(n)`: Move the cursor along the grid, `n` steps.
- `paw.curves.editor.nudge_point(n)`: Raise or lower the point under the cursor `n` steps.
- `paw.curves.editor.open(uri, opts)`: Show a curve: in the window that shows it already, else in a new window split below the current one (beside it with `opts.vertical`), or in this window with `opts.here`. With `opts.window` in a graphical frontend's window of its own. `opts.beat` puts the cursor there.
- `paw.curves.editor.paste(register, count)`: Put the points of a register at the cursor, over what is there.
- `paw.curves.editor.picture(g, px, t, points, s)`: The plot in pixels (a strip under the cells, `buf:strip`): the grid, the curve and the area under it, through `paw.plot`. A value is as high as the middle of the dot the cells would put it in (`s.sub` dots a cell down, as `paw.opt.curve_glyphs` has them), so that the points and the cursor, drawn in cells over it, sit on the line.
- `paw.curves.editor.remove(n)`: Remove `n` points from the one under the cursor on.
- `paw.curves.editor.target(win)`: The curve a window shows, or nil and why not.
- `paw.curves.editor.tension(by)`: Bend the smooth stretch from the point under the cursor.
- `paw.curves.editor.to_end(dir)`: To the first (`dir` -1) or last point.
- `paw.curves.editor.to_point(dir, n)`: To the next point (`dir` 1) or the one before, `n` times; the cursor takes its value.
- `paw.curves.editor.type_value()`: Type the value of the point under the cursor, or of a new one there.
- `paw.curves.editor.under_cursor(note)`: The curve of what the cursor is on in the focused view: a lane row or the tempo lane in the arrange view, a parameter in the device panel, the strip's controller in the piano roll (with `note`, that of the note under the cursor alone). Nil and why not when it is on none.
- `paw.curves.editor.wave_menu(from, to, where)`: The wave menu, then the wave over a region.
- `paw.curves.editor.zoom(factor)`: Zoom the editor's window in or out by `factor`.

## Module paw.diagnostic

- `paw.diagnostic.about(d, uri)`: Whether a diagnostic is about an address or something it holds: a note counts when a diagnostic of its clip names it among its notes.
- `paw.diagnostic.actions(target, place)`: The fixes of the diagnostics about a place (as `get` takes its target and filter), as `{ title, diagnostic, fix, run }`, the most severe first. `actions(clip, place)` asks about one note of a clip.
- `paw.diagnostic.apply(d, fix)`: Carry out a fix of a diagnostic as one undo step. Returns whether it did.
- `paw.diagnostic.config(opts)`: Change how diagnostics are shown; returns the options in force.

  ```lua
  paw.diagnostic.config({ virtual_text = false })
  ```
- `paw.diagnostic.count(target, filter)`: How many diagnostics of each severity (as `get` takes its target): `{ error = 1, warning = 2, info = 0, hint = 0, total = 3 }`.
- `paw.diagnostic.format(d)`: A diagnostic in one line: `warning parallel-perfect: Parallel fifths … [midi-lsp]`.
- `paw.diagnostic.get(target, filter)`: Diagnostics, sorted by kind and then by where they are. `target`: a clip id (those about it and its notes), an address (those about it or what it holds), or nil for all. `filter`: `namespace`, `severity` (a severity or `{ min, max }`, min the least severe), `note` (a place in the clip), `kind` (as `paw.diagnostic.kind`), `document`.
- `paw.diagnostic.goto_next(opts)`: Go to the next diagnostic, or `opts.count` on (`]d`).
- `paw.diagnostic.goto_prev(opts)`: Go to the diagnostic before, or `opts.count` back (`[d`).
- `paw.diagnostic.group(prefix, severity)`: The highlight group for a severity with a prefix: `Diagnostic` gives `DiagnosticWarn`.
- `paw.diagnostic.jump(dir, count)`: The next (`dir` 1) or previous (-1) diagnostic the focused view can place, from its cursor, `count` times, round the ends; the cursor goes there. Returns it, or nil when the view has none.
- `paw.diagnostic.kind(d)`: The kind of thing a diagnostic is about, for grouping: clip, track, device, time, project, render, or an extension's kind.
- `paw.diagnostic.list(target)`: Every diagnostic (of `target`, as `get` takes it) in a picker, as the quickfix list, grouped by what they are about: Enter goes to one.
- `paw.diagnostic.marks()`: What the window marks elsewhere: each track (by id) with the worst said of it, its devices or sends, and the first message; and the stretches of time.
- `paw.diagnostic.namespaces()`: The namespaces that have published anything.
- `paw.diagnostic.notes_of(d)`: The notes of a diagnostic as they are now.
- `paw.diagnostic.paint_part(p, id, offset)`: One clip's, `offset` beats from the roll's own.
- `paw.diagnostic.paint_roll(p)`: Mark the diagnostics of every clip the piano roll edits, as one of its layers: each note underlined in its severity's colour, the message after the last note while there is room, and a mark on the ruler where it starts.
- `paw.diagnostic.places(d)`: The places the notes of a diagnostic have now (from 1); a note that has gone is left out.
- `paw.diagnostic.reset(namespace, doc)`: Forget what `namespace` said, about one document (or, given a clip id, everything it said about that clip) or all; with no namespace, everything anyone said about that, or everything.
- `paw.diagnostic.roll_marks(id)`: What the window marks in its piano roll for a clip: each note a diagnostic is about, by place from 0, with its worst severity, the messages about it and the titles of the fixes for it.
- `paw.diagnostic.set(namespace, doc, list)`: Publish what `namespace` says about a document (a clip, or any string: a server's document URI), replacing what it said of it before. An empty list clears it.
- `paw.diagnostic.setloclist(opts)`: The diagnostics in the current window's location list.
- `paw.diagnostic.setqflist(opts)`: Put the diagnostics in the quickfix list, as `vim.diagnostic.setqflist`: `opts` has `target`, `severity` (the least severe), `title`, `open`. `setloclist` puts them in the current window's location list.
- `paw.diagnostic.severity_of(value)`: A severity from 1 (error) to 4 (hint), from a number or a word.
- `paw.diagnostic.show(d)`: Put the cursor of the view that shows it best on a diagnostic, and say it.
- `paw.diagnostic.status()`: The status line's piece: `E1 W2` for the clip in the piano roll, or the whole project when none is open. Nil when there is nothing to say.
- `paw.diagnostic.where(d)`: Where a diagnostic is about, in a few words: `Lead › Synth · cutoff`, `chords 2.1.00`, `5.1.00–9.1.00`, `mix.wav`.
- `paw.diagnostic.worst(uri, filter)`: The worst severity said about an address or what it holds, or nil.

## Module paw.draw

- `paw.draw.bar_lines(from, span)`: The bars and beats from `from` for `span` beats, as the project counts them: `{ beat = b, bar = n }` for a bar line (n from 1) and `{ beat = b }` for a beat inside a bar. Bar lines come from `paw.time.bar_start`, so a change of time signature moves them.
- `paw.draw.beats(ruler, scroll, span, zoom, origin)`: Number a ruler above a roll that shows `span` beats from `scroll` at `zoom` columns a beat: bars as the project counts them (`origin` is the project beat of the roll's beat 0), beats in between as ticks. Returns where the lines go, as `{ x, bar }`, for the rows underneath.
- `paw.draw.braille(bits)`: A braille character from its eight dots: bit k is dot k + 1.
- `paw.draw.chips(buf, x, y, list, gap)`: Small on/off marks side by side, each a letter on a cell of its own: `chips(buf, x, y, { { "M", on, "Mute" }, ... }, gap)`. Returns the columns used.
- `paw.draw.clear_peak(id)`: Put out a track's clip light and let its loudest of late fall.
- `paw.draw.curve(buf, y, rows, value, style)`: Draw a curve as a thin line over `rows` rows of a buffer, from row `y` down: `value(i)` gives the height, from 0 at the bottom to 1 at the top, at the `i`th of two points per column. Only the cells the line passes through are touched. Sextants (a connected line), braille dots or lines at three heights a row, as `M.curve_glyphs()` says.
- `paw.draw.curve_glyphs()`: How curves are drawn in cells: "sextant", "braille" or "line", by `paw.opt.curve_glyphs`; `paw.opt.braille = false` and `paw.opt.ascii` both mean "line" (ascii wins over all, and uses ASCII characters).
- `paw.draw.db_cell(db, width)`: Where on a meter `width` cells long a level in dB falls, from 0.
- `paw.draw.db_text(db)`: A volume in dB as few cells as it can: `-4.0`, `-inf`, `+2.5`.
- `paw.draw.hold(key, peak)`: Peaks held for a while, by key: `hold(key, peak)` gives the loudest of the last two seconds, which falls back once that time has passed.
- `paw.draw.hue(colour)`: Highlight groups in the shades of one colour (`#rrggbb`), made the first time the colour is asked for:

  ```lua
  fg                  the colour itself, on whatever is behind it
  title, body         a clip's name row and the rows under it
  title_cur, body_cur the same for the clip under the cursor (or chosen)
  title_off, body_off the same for a muted clip
  lane_sel            the background of the selected track's lane
  note, note_soft, note_faint   notes, loud to quiet
  pill                dark text on the colour
  plate               a name plate: light text on a deep shade
  ```
- `paw.draw.keys(buf, x, y, entries, width, groups)`: A row of keys and what they do, for a line of hints: `{ { "o", "new track" }, ... }`, joined by a faint dot. `? keys` always comes last when it is in the list. Returns the columns used; entries that do not fit are left out.
- `paw.draw.level(peak)`: How far up a meter a linear peak reaches, from 0 to 1 over 60 dB.
- `paw.draw.meter(buf, x, y, width, peak, hold)`: A level meter `width` cells wide for a linear peak: a thin rail, lit from the left, green then yellow then red. With `hold` (a linear peak), the loudest of late is marked.
- `paw.draw.miniroll(notes, width, rows, zoom, from)`: Notes as a small piano roll of `rows` text rows, each `width` columns: two pitches' worth of height to a row, drawn with half blocks. `notes` have `start`, `length` and `pitch`; a column covers `1 / zoom` beats from `from`.
- `paw.draw.mix(a, b, t)`: A colour between two: `t` 0 gives `a`, 1 gives `b`.
- `paw.draw.nearest256(hex)`: The nearest of the 256 colours to `#rrggbb`, from the 6x6x6 cube (16 to 231) or the greys (232 to 255), a grey for any colour with little hue: its index and the colour it stands for.
- `paw.draw.note_style(hue, velocity)`: The shade of a note by how hard it is played.
- `paw.draw.pan(buf, x, y, width, pan, style)`: A pan from -1 to 1 as a bar `width` cells wide (odd is best): a rail with a mark where the sound sits, `───┃───` in the middle.
- `paw.draw.pan_text(pan)`: Where a pan from -1 to 1 points, in a few cells: `L30`, `C`, `R100`.
- `paw.draw.piano_key(buf, row, pitch, cursor, width, name)`: One row of a keyboard on its side, `width` cells wide, for the left edge of a piano roll: black keys are short, the Cs are named, and so is the pitch the cursor is on.
- `paw.draw.reset()`: Forget the shades made so far: after the palette has changed.
- `paw.draw.sextant(bits)`: The character for a set of sextants (U+1FB00 to U+1FB3B, two columns by three rows): bits 1 to 32 are top left, top right, middle left, middle right, bottom left, bottom right. The patterns that are not in that block are a space, the left half, the right half and the full block.
- `paw.draw.slider(buf, x, y, width, fraction, on, off)`: A slider `width` cells wide with its knob `fraction` of the way along.
- `paw.draw.stereo_meter(buf, x, y, width, left, right)`: Both sides of a stereo level in one row `width` cells wide: the left in the upper half of each cell, the right in the lower.
- `paw.draw.term_def(def, truecolor)`: A highlight definition as this terminal can show it: on one without 24-bit colour, each `#rrggbb` becomes the nearest of the 256.
- `paw.draw.trace(width, samples, y, sub, kind)`: A connected line over a grid of cells, for a curve: `y(sx)` gives the row of the line, from the top, in `sub` rows a cell (3 for sextants, 4 for braille), at the `sx`th of two samples a cell, from 0, or nil for none; `samples` of them. A jump is filled from the last row to this one, so that the line is unbroken. Returns `{ [row * width + col] = bits }`, the bits as `M.sextant` or `M.braille` take them.
- `paw.draw.track_colour(track, index)`: The colour of a track: its own if it has one, else one of the theme's by its place in the track list.
- `paw.draw.track_hue(track, index)`: The hue of a track's colour, from 0 to 360.
- `paw.draw.track_peak(id)`: A track's meter as the mixer shows it, in a terminal and in a window (`scene.live`): both sides, the loudest of late and whether it has reached full scale since `clear_peak` was last called for it.
- `paw.draw.truecolor()`: Whether the terminal shows 24-bit colour: `paw.opt.termcolors` "true" or "256", or with "auto" (the default) what the environment says: COLORTERM of truecolor or 24bit, or a TERM that ends in -direct.
- `paw.draw.use_glyphs()`: Take the glyphs `paw.opt.ascii` asks for into `paw.draw.g`.
- `paw.draw.vmeter(buf, x, y, height, peak, hold)`: A level meter `height` cells tall, lit from the bottom, with the peak held (`hold`, linear) marked by a line over its cell.
- `paw.draw.wave_reach(a)`: How far a sample of size `a` (0 to 1) reaches up a waveform, 0 to 1: as it is (`paw.opt.wave_scale` "linear", which shows a kick over a hat) or on a decibel scale from -48 (`"db"`, which shows quiet material).
- `paw.draw.waveform(peaks, rows)`: Peaks (`{ min, max }` pairs from -1 to 1, one per column) as a waveform of `rows` text rows, each column drawn from its lowest to its highest sample around the middle of the rows, in eighths of a row. Returns the rows as text and, for each row, its runs `{ column, text, mark }` of cells that share a mark, the column counted from 0 (the text of a run is drawn with the mark's style, `nil` for none): "flip" is for cells whose upper part is the wave, an eighth block drawn in reverse video because blocks only grow from the bottom, "clip" for a column that reaches full scale, "clipflip" for both.

## Module paw.events

- `paw.events.emit`: the same as `paw.emit`.
- `paw.events.handlers()`: Every handler, by its handle: `{ pattern, fn }`.
- `paw.events.listened(name)`: Whether anything listens for `name` by its name or its family (`*` aside): for events that cost something to work out.
- `paw.events.off`: the same as `paw.off`.
- `paw.events.on`: the same as `paw.on`.
- `paw.events.once`: the same as `paw.once`.

## Module paw.ex

- `paw.ex.address_of(item)`: The address of an item, for the quickfix list and for going to it.
- `paw.ex.apply(changes, remove)`: Make the changes `{ item, change }` and remove the items in `remove`, as one edit per clip.
- `paw.ex.change(item, sets, pattern)`: What a replacement makes of one item: the fields that change, as `paw.api` keeps them.
- `paw.ex.complete_pattern(line)`: Field names as they are typed in a pattern: `:%s/ve` offers `vel`.
- `paw.ex.complete_range(line)`: What could finish a range being typed: marks after `'`, tracks after `t/`. Nil when the line is not in the middle of one.
- `paw.ex.describe(r)`: What a range covers, in words: "bars 5–8 on 2 tracks".
- `paw.ex.exec(line, ctx)`: Run a command line, as typed after `:`, with a range in front if it has one. A line with a range, or an Ex command, is one undo step named after the line (a line typed after `:` always is).
- `paw.ex.field(name, spec)`: A field that `:s` and `:g` patterns can name (`lyric:la`): `level` (note, clip or track), `type`, `get(item)`, `set(item, value, change)`.
- `paw.ex.go(r)`: Move to where a range starts, as `:5` does in Vim.
- `paw.ex.item_of(uri)`: The item an address names, or nil.
- `paw.ex.items(r, kind)`: The notes, clips or tracks (`kind`) a range holds, in the order they come in the song.
- `paw.ex.label(item)`: An item in a few words: "C4 vel 100 at 5.1.00 in Verse".
- `paw.ex.mark(state, item, change)`: Remember an item for the views: lit, and with its change as a ghost.
- `paw.ex.pattern(text)`: Read a pattern: `{ text, level, test(item), names = { substrings of names it looks for } }`.
- `paw.ex.preview(text)`: Show what a line typed so far would do: called by the command line as it changes, and with nil when it closes. Returns a few words for the command line, and "error" when they say what is wrong.
- `paw.ex.range(line)`: Split a range off the front of a command line: the range, and the rest. Nil for the range when there is none; an error message as the third value instead of the rest when the range names nothing.
- `paw.ex.replacement(text, pattern)`: Read a replacement for what `pattern` matches: a list of changes, or an empty list, which removes what matched.
- `paw.ex.selection_range()`: The last selection of the focused view as a range of the song.
- `paw.ex.show(item)`: Put the cursor on an item, in the view that shows it.
- `paw.ex.shown()`: What the views show now, for frontends and tests: `{ from, to, tracks, matches, notes, clips, current }`, or nil.
- `paw.ex.split(rest)`: Split what follows a range into the command's name, the text after it, and how many times a `>` or `<` was typed.
- `paw.ex.substitution(r, pattern, replacement, flags)`: What a substitution would do: the matches, the ones it changes, and for each its change (false to remove it).
- `paw.ex.view(name, spec)`: Say how a view of your own maps its columns to the song's beats and which clips it edits, for ranges: see docs/scripting.md.

## Module paw.ext

- `paw.ext.bundled()`: The names of the bundled extensions, loaded or not, sorted.
- `paw.ext.bundled_dir()`: The directory of the extensions that come with the program: `$PAW_HOME/extensions`, or `extensions` under the working directory in a source tree. Nil when neither is there.
- `paw.ext.list()`: Loaded extensions, sorted by name.
- `paw.ext.load(path)`: Load one extension from a directory or a `.lua` file. One the program was built with is not loaded again from elsewhere: the configuration that names the source tree's copy gets the packaged one.
- `paw.ext.load_bundled(name)`: Load a bundled extension by name; a name already loaded is left alone. Returns the entry, or nil and what is wrong.
- `paw.ext.load_dir(dir)`: Load everything in a directory of extensions.
- `paw.ext.load_packaged(dirs)`: Load the extensions the program was built with: `dirs` is a list of their directories separated by `:` (`$PAW_EXTENSIONS`, which the flake's `paw.withExtensions` sets).
- `paw.ext.manifest(path, name)`: An extension's manifest: `manifest.lua` in its directory. A one-file extension has none. Returns the table (with `name` filled in), or nil and what is wrong with it.
- `paw.ext.parse_version(text)`: A version's numbers: "1.2.3" gives { 1, 2, 3 }; missing parts are 0. Nil for text that is no version.
- `paw.ext.provides(name)`: What a loaded extension registered: a list of `{ kind, title, items }`, each item a short label, in the order of `paw.ext.registries`.
- `paw.ext.satisfies(version, want)`: Whether `version` meets `want`: comparisons separated by spaces or commas, each `>=1.2`, `>1`, `<=2`, `<2.0`, `=1.2.3`, `^1.2` (the same first number, at least 1.2), `~1.2` (the same first two) or a bare version, which means `^`. `*` or nothing is any version.
- `paw.ext.unload(name)`: Take an extension away: everything it registered while it loaded is removed, and what it replaced put back (a command or key of the core it remapped). Its modules are forgotten, so loading it again runs them afresh. Options it defined keep their defaults; devices it ships stay among the devices for the session. Returns true, or nil and why not.

## Module paw.files

- `paw.files.buffer_name(dir, tree)`: The name of the buffer that lists a folder, as a tree or not.
- `paw.files.is_dir(path)`: Whether a path is a folder.
- `paw.files.open(dir, opts)`: Show a folder: in this window (`opts.here`), or split beside (a tree by default). `opts.tree`, `opts.filter` ("unused") and `opts.hidden`.
- `paw.files.sound_info(path, stat)`: What a sound file's header says: `{ rate, channels, seconds }`, or nil for a file that is not one that can be read.
- `paw.files.watch()`: Start watching the cursor, once a files buffer exists.

## Module paw.freeze

- `paw.freeze.freeze(track, opts)`: Freeze a track or a group: render it, and play the file from now on. `opts.tail` is the seconds rendered after the song's end (2). One undo step. Returns the file.
- `paw.freeze.frozen(track)`: What a frozen track was frozen to, `{ file }`, or nil.
- `paw.freeze.holder(track)`: The frozen track a track sounds through, if any: the one whose file holds its sound.
- `paw.freeze.render_opts(track, opts)`: The options a freeze renders with: the whole song from its start, the track alone before its fader, as 32-bit float, so that the file plays what the track did.
- `paw.freeze.state(track)`: "frozen", "held" (its sound is in a frozen track it feeds), or nil.
- `paw.freeze.unfreeze(track)`: Play a frozen track's clips and devices again. The file stays where it is, as undo can bring the freeze back.

## Module paw.frontend

- `paw.frontend.band_state()`: The bands that have entries, as rows from 0 under the marker band: `{ rows, entries }`, each entry with its `row`, its `band` and `index` (for `act.band`), `beat`, `length`, `name`, `color`, `active` and `hint`.
- `paw.frontend.choose_clips(set)`: Choose a set of clips (`{ [id] = true }`), as visual mode's selection: what `:select` does.
- `paw.frontend.choose_notes(clip, places)`: Choose notes of `clip` by their places (`{ [place] = true }`), as the pointer would: what `:select` does.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_clips()`: The ids of the chosen clips, in order.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_notes(clip)`: The places of the chosen notes of `clip`, in order; none if the clip's notes have changed under them.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_refs()`: Every chosen note of the clips the roll edits, as `{ clip, place }`.
- `paw.frontend.chosen_text(clip)`: The chosen notes of `clip` (and of the clips edited with it) in words, for a toolbar: "3 notes · 5.1.00 – 5.3.00", or "" with none chosen.
- `paw.frontend.clip(id)`: One clip with its notes and controller moves, for a piano roll, and the name and colour of the track it is on. Nil when the clip is gone.
- `paw.frontend.closing()`: Whether closing now would lose anything: { modified, name, path }.
- `paw.frontend.completions(prompt)`: The candidates a prompt offers, as the terminal lists them above the line: the ones in view around the one chosen, `{ label, desc }`, with `chosen` the place of the one chosen among them (0 for none).
- `paw.frontend.dialog_info()`: What the window needs to open the desktop's own file dialog: `native`, whether to (the option, and the dialogs shown are the kernel's own when the window is turned off), `dir`, where to start (where a file was last chosen, else beside the project, else home: as the list picker does), `name`, the project's file name, for "Save as", and `render`, the endings a render can write.
- `paw.frontend.engine_menu()`: The menu where the audio devices are chosen: `info` (lines to show), `output`, `input`, `block`, `rate` and `backend`, each a list of `{ label, checked }`. `act.choose_engine` takes one by heading and place.
- `paw.frontend.float(width, height)`: The floating window that is open (help, a list, a picker), drawn as text `width` columns wide: its title and its lines. Nil when there is none.
- `paw.frontend.format_value(param, value)`: A parameter's value as text in its unit (see `paw.params.format`).
- `paw.frontend.input_menu(track)`: The menu of a track's input: the choices of `paw.audio.choices` under their headings, `audio`, `midi` and `channel`, and where the track sends MIDI, `midi_out`, `midi_out_channel` and `midi_out_form`, each a list of `{ label, checked }`. `act.choose_input` takes one by heading and place.
- `paw.frontend.lane_name(lane)`: What a lane moves, in words: `Volume`, `Pan`, `Synth · cutoff`.
- `paw.frontend.lane_span(lane)`: The stretch of a lane's range that is worth drawing it over: a fader's travel for volume, the whole range for anything else.
- `paw.frontend.launch_state(ids)`: What each drawn track (`ids`, the master last) plays from its slots, by place: `slot` and `queued` are rows or -1, `stopping` and `back` say a stop or a return to the timeline is queued, `stopped` that it plays nothing, `progress` how far round its loop the clip is (0 to 1), and `recording` the row being recorded into or -1. Empty while nothing is launched or recorded anywhere.
- `paw.frontend.layout_get()`: How the window was left (its size, the zoom, the heights of rows and of the piano roll, whether the mixer shows): a table, empty when nothing was kept. It belongs to the machine, so it is kept here, where a window attached to this kernel finds it too. (`M.layout_path` names another file, for tests.)
- `paw.frontend.layout_set(layout)`: Keep the window's layout (see `layout_get`).
- `paw.frontend.menu(kind, args)`: Menu `kind` for `args`, as plain data for a window to show.
- `paw.frontend.outputs_menu(device)`: The menu of a device's further output pairs: for each, `{ label, choices }`, where the label names the pair and where it plays and the choices (`{ label, checked }`) are "Nowhere" and the tracks it can play into. `act.route_pair` takes one; `act.spread_outputs` makes a track for each pair that plays nowhere.
- `paw.frontend.peaks(clip, points)`: The waveform of an audio clip at `points` points (`M.peak_points` without), as one flat list { min1, max1, rms1, min2, max2, rms2, ... }: how far the wave reaches each way and how loud it is, which is its body. Kept out of `state`, which is sent again whenever the cursor moves, so that a frontend fetches each waveform once for each width it draws at.
- `paw.frontend.preview(id)`: A MIDI clip's notes for the small picture inside it: one flat list { start1, length1, pitch1, start2, ... }, at most `M.preview_notes` notes. Fetched when the clip's `stamp` in `state` changes.
- `paw.frontend.recent_menu()`: The recent projects the File menu lists: `{ label, path }` each.
- `paw.frontend.refresh()`: Have the frontend fetch the project's state again, though nothing in the project has changed: for what an extension adds to it.
- `paw.frontend.render_dialog()`: What the render dialog starts from: the file a render would go to, the ranges that can be rendered (`{ name, label }`: the song, the loop, the selection, every region), the engine's sample rate, and which lossy formats ffmpeg can make here (`formats`: `{ mp3 = true, ogg = false, ... }`).
- `paw.frontend.roll_chords(clip)`: The chord symbols over a clip, as `paw.opt.chords` asks for them: `{ start, length, label }` in the clip's beats; none when it is off.
- `paw.frontend.routing(track)`: Where a track's sound goes, for a frontend to show and change:

  ```lua
  output   the name of the track it plays into ("Master" without one)
  targets  the tracks it could play into or send to, `{ id, name }` each;
           the master is first, with id 0
  sends    `{ target, name, level, pre }` each, levels in dB
  ```

  A track cannot play into itself or into a track that plays into it.
- `paw.frontend.save_as(after)`: Save the project under a new name: choose the directory from a list, then type the file's name. `after` runs once it is saved.
- `paw.frontend.send_list(track)`: A track's sends as `{ name, level }`, the level in dB.
- `paw.frontend.sidechain_menu(device)`: The menu of a device's side-chain: "None" first, then the tracks it can listen to, then whether it is taken before their fader; each `{ label, checked }`. `act.choose_sidechain` takes one by place.
- `paw.frontend.slots(ids)`: The clips in the drawn tracks' slots: `{ id, track, row, name, midi, mode, legato, quantize, muted }` each, `track` by place from 0.
- `paw.frontend.state(known)`: What a graphical frontend is told: transport, tracks, clips, devices and the modal state, as plain data; `known` lists what it already has.
- `paw.frontend.step_input()`: Whether step input (notes entered from a MIDI keyboard) is on.
- `paw.frontend.take_preview(id, take, points)`: What take `take` of a clip plays, for the picture in its take lane: a waveform as `M.peaks` gives one at `points` points for sound, the notes as `M.preview` gives them for MIDI, repeated as a looped clip repeats. The playing take's waveform is the clip's own, stretched; another's is its file squeezed or spread in time as far as the clip stretches it.
- `paw.frontend.take_rows(clip)`: A clip's takes as its take lanes show them: `{ name, key }` each, `key` changing exactly when what the take plays does. Nil for a clip without takes, which has nothing in the lanes.
- `paw.frontend.vca_words(id)`: What a track is in VCA terms, for a strip: a VCA's members by name, a member's VCAs by name, joined by commas.

## Module paw.fx

- `paw.fx.add(track, kind, opts)`: Add a device as a person does, from the device picker, the window's "Add a device" box or `:device.add`: like `track:add_device`, and then a plugin with a window of its own shows it (`paw.opt.editor_on_add`), as REAPER does. Some instruments make no sound until it has been open once.
- `paw.fx.added(device, kind, opts)`: The second half of `add`, once the device is there: remembered as used, its window shown.
- `paw.fx.card_params(d)`: A device's own parameters in the order its card shows them: the ones chosen, the one last touched, then the rest. `d` is `api.device_get`'s.
- `paw.fx.current(device)`: The name of the preset the device was last set to, if any.
- `paw.fx.default_preset(kind)`: The preset new instances of a kind start from, if the user marked one.
- `paw.fx.delete(kind, name)`: Delete a preset of a kind of device, by name.
- `paw.fx.device_line(info)`: The line a device is listed with: a star for a favourite, then its name, vendor, the extension it came with if one did, its format and whether it is an instrument or an effect.
- `paw.fx.device_list(wanted)`: Every device that can be added: favourites first, then the ones used last, newest first, then the rest (the kind `wanted` first, see `preferred`; built-in ones first, by name).
- `paw.fx.factory_presets(device)`: The device's own presets: a plugin's, or a built-in device's from `paw.fx.factory`. `{ name, category, id }`, in the order the plugin gives.
- `paw.fx.focus_param(id, key)`: Put the device panel's row on one parameter of a device.
- `paw.fx.hide_param(device, key)`: Take a parameter off the device's card in the window.
- `paw.fx.interactive()`: Whether a person is at the program: a terminal UI is attached, or a graphical frontend has asked for the state lately. Scripts (`-l`) and a kernel nobody is looking at are not.
- `paw.fx.is_favourite(kind)`: Whether a kind of device is a favourite.
- `paw.fx.learn(device, param)`: Learn a controller for a device's parameter: the next one moved moves it.
- `paw.fx.library()`: What is kept about kinds of device across sessions (`favourites`), read once.
- `paw.fx.load(device, preset)`: Load a preset into the device by name (the user's first), or one from `paw.fx.presets(device)`. One undo step.
- `paw.fx.note_used(kind, query)`: Note that a device was chosen, after `query` was typed if anything.
- `paw.fx.pick(device)`: Choose a preset of the device in a picker and load it.
- `paw.fx.pick_param(device)`: Choose one of the device's parameters by typing part of its name: it is shown first on the window's card and chosen in the device panel.
- `paw.fx.place(track, kind, opts)`: The first half of `add`: the device on the track, set to the preset new ones start from. What the device picker tries out before it is chosen.
- `paw.fx.preferred(track_id)`: Which kind of device a track most likely wants next: "instrument" for one that makes sound from MIDI and has no instrument yet, "effect" for the rest (a track with an instrument, the master, a track of audio).
- `paw.fx.presets(device)`: Every preset of the device: the user's first, then the factory's.
- `paw.fx.presets_dir()`: Where presets are kept: `paw.opt.presets_dir`, or `presets` in the data directory.
- `paw.fx.rank(info, query, line, wanted)`: How well a device matches what was typed, or nil when it does not: the `@` words filter, the rest is matched against the whole line, a match in the name alone counts for more than one that needs the vendor, and the device chosen last time for the same words comes first. A device of the category `wanted` (see `preferred`) comes before others.
- `paw.fx.reload_library()`: Forget what was read, for tests that change the file underneath.
- `paw.fx.save(device, name)`: Save the device as it is now as a user preset. Returns the file's path.
- `paw.fx.search(query, limit, wanted)`: The devices matching `query`, best first, at most `limit`: what the window's "Add a device" box lists.
- `paw.fx.select(id)`: Put the device panel's row on a device of the cursor track.
- `paw.fx.set_default(kind, name)`: Mark the preset that new instances of `kind` start from, or none.
