- `paw.fx.set_gain(device, db)`: A device's own gain after its effect, in dB.
- `paw.fx.set_wet(device, percent)`: How much of a device's effect is heard, in percent.
- `paw.fx.setup()`: Define the commands for devices. The runtime calls this once at start.
- `paw.fx.show_param(device, key)`: Show a parameter first on the device's card; kept with the device.
- `paw.fx.shown(device)`: The keys of the parameters the user chose to show for a device.
- `paw.fx.step(device, step)`: Load the next (`step` 1) or previous (-1) preset of the device's list.
- `paw.fx.target()`: The device the preset commands act on: the one selected in the device panel (its row stays where it was when another view has the keys).
- `paw.fx.toggle_favourite(kind)`: Make a kind of device a favourite, or not; returns whether it is now.
- `paw.fx.user_presets(kind)`: The user's presets for a kind of device, by name: `{ name, path }`.

## Module paw.grep

- `paw.grep.entries(records)`: Records as quickfix entries: `lyric: la`.
- `paw.grep.fields()`: The fields text can be found in, for completion.
- `paw.grep.matcher(pattern, mode)`: A test of text: `mode` "regex" (`paw.regex`), "exact" (the words, each anywhere) or "fuzzy" (as the pickers match). Raises an error for a bad regular expression.
- `paw.grep.records()`: Every record of every source, in the order the sources were added. A source that fails is passed over and logged.
- `paw.grep.search(pattern, opts)`: The records whose text matches `pattern`; `opts.mode` as `matcher` takes it, `opts.fields` a set of fields to look in (all without it).
- `paw.grep.source(name, fn)`: Add a source of text, or replace the one of that name.
- `paw.grep.vimgrep(arg, opts)`: What `:vimgrep` does: search, fill the list, go to the first place found unless the flags hold `j`. `opts.loc` the window's location list, `opts.add` adds to the current list. Returns the records found.

## Module paw.groups

- `paw.groups.add(track, group)`: Put a track into a group: it then sounds through the group, unless it was sent somewhere of its own.
- `paw.groups.depth(track)`: How many groups a track is inside.
- `paw.groups.dissolve(group)`: Undo a group: its members go up a level and the group, if it holds nothing of its own (no clips, no devices), goes away.
- `paw.groups.fold(group, on)`: Fold a group away, or open it: `on` nil flips it.
- `paw.groups.folded(group)`: Whether a group's tracks are folded out of sight.
- `paw.groups.gather(group)`: Put a group's members right under it, in the order they are in.
- `paw.groups.hidden(track, top)`: Whether a track is out of sight: inside a group that is folded. Seen from inside group `top` (a narrowed tab's), only the groups inside it count: `top` itself is open there.
- `paw.groups.is_group(track)`: Whether a track is a group.
- `paw.groups.link(group, on)`: Link the faders of a group's members, or let them go: `on` nil flips it.
- `paw.groups.linked(group)`: Whether the faders of a group's members are linked: moving one moves the others by as many dB. This is apart from routing, which a group has too.
- `paw.groups.make(tracks, name)`: A new group holding `tracks` (ids or tracks), above the first of them. Returns the group's track.
- `paw.groups.members(group)`: The tracks that belong to a group, in the order of the track list.
- `paw.groups.of(track)`: The group a track belongs to (its id), or nil.
- `paw.groups.remove(track, stay)`: Take a track out of its group, up a level: it sounds where the group sounds, and belongs to the group that one is in, if any. It moves out of the group's block of rows, unless `stay`.
- `paw.groups.rows(opts)`: The tracks that are drawn, in order: all but those folded away, and in a narrowed tab only those of its group (`paw.scope`). Rows of the arrange view and of a graphical frontend are places in this list. With `{ lanes = true }`, every row: `{ track = id }` for a track and `{ track = id, lane = id }` for an automation lane shown under it (see `paw.lanes`).

## Module paw.harmony

- `paw.harmony.at(beat)`: The chord sounding at `beat`, or nil.
- `paw.harmony.builtin(from, to)`: The built-in provider: chords and keys read from the notes.
- `paw.harmony.chord_name(chord, key)`: A chord's symbol: "G7", "F/A", "Bbmaj7", spelled as `key` writes it.
- `paw.harmony.chord_roman(chord, key)`: A chord's Roman numeral in `key`, counted from the tonic as in the major scale ("bVII", "vi", "V7", "ii°"); an inversion as "V7/B" is left to the name.
- `paw.harmony.chords(from, to)`: The chords that sound between `from` and `to` (project beats; all of them when nil), in time order.
- `paw.harmony.degree(key, pitch)`: A pitch as an absolute scale degree (0 is the root in octave -1) and the semitones it lies above that degree (non-zero for notes outside it).
- `paw.harmony.degree_pitch(key, degree)`: The pitch of an absolute scale degree.
- `paw.harmony.draw(buf, scroll, span, zoom, origin, how)`: Draw the chords on a row of cells: `buf` one row high, showing `span` beats from `scroll` at `zoom` columns a beat, beats counted from `origin` (a clip's start; 0 for the song). Each symbol starts on the left edge of the cell where its chord starts, and is cut short where the next one starts. Labels as `paw.opt.chords` (or `how`) asks.
- `paw.harmony.fresh()`: Whether the reading is up to date with the project, so that `key` and `chords` answer at once: a view drawn on every key asks this first, as reading a long song again takes a while.
- `paw.harmony.in_key(key, pitch)`: Whether a pitch (or pitch class) belongs to a key.
- `paw.harmony.invalidate()`: Forget the reading: a provider whose answer changed calls this.
- `paw.harmony.is_drums(track)`: Whether a track is left out of the harmony: a drum track (a drum map in its meta, as the drums extension keeps it, or a drum device or name).
- `paw.harmony.key(beat)`: The key at `beat` (the start when nil): the project's when one is set, else the one read there, else C major. `{ tonic, mode, name, ... }`.
- `paw.harmony.key_name(key)`: "D minor", "Bb major": the tonic spelled as its key writes it.
- `paw.harmony.keys()`: The keys read over the song, `{ at, length, tonic, mode, name }` each; the project's own key, when one is set, over all of it.
- `paw.harmony.label(chord, how)`: A chord's label as `paw.opt.chords` (or `how`) asks: its name, its numeral, or both ("G7 V7").
- `paw.harmony.next(beat)`: The first chord that starts after `beat`.
- `paw.harmony.notes()`: Every note of the pitched tracks, in project beats, each with `track` and `clip`. Muted clips and tracks are left out; so are notes hidden by a trim of the clip's edges. Kept until the project changes: this is what sounds, for the reading and for snippets alike. (The piano roll's context notes, `paw.roll_clips.context`, are what it shows, in its own beats and only of the tracks chosen to show.)
- `paw.harmony.parse_chord(text)`: A chord from its symbol: "G7", "F#m7b5", "C/E", "Bbmaj7". Nil when it is not one.
- `paw.harmony.parse_key(spec)`: A key from a name ("D minor", "F# dorian", "Bb") or a table (`{ root = "D", scale = "minor" }`, `{ tonic = 2, mode = "minor" }`, or a key). A key is `{ tonic, mode, name, root = tonic, scale = mode, steps }`.
- `paw.harmony.pc_name(pc, key)`: The name of a pitch class: spelled as `key` writes it (sharps or flats), else the names most often written (C#, Eb, F#, Ab, Bb).
- `paw.harmony.pitch_class(name)`: A pitch class (0..11) from a name such as "C", "f#", "Bb", or a number.
- `paw.harmony.prev(beat)`: The last chord that starts before `beat` and is not the one at it.
- `paw.harmony.project_key()`: The key set for the project, or nil when none is.
- `paw.harmony.provide(name, fn, priority)`: Add a provider: `fn(from, to)` returns chords and keys (lists in the shapes `chords` and `key` give; `root`, `quality`, `at`, `length` are enough for a chord, `at`, `length`, `tonic`, `mode` for a key), or nil to leave it to the next. The highest `priority` (default 50) asks first. Providing again under a name replaces it; `fn` nil removes it.
- `paw.harmony.provider()`: The provider the current reading came from.
- `paw.harmony.range(track)`: The range a part for a track is written in, `{ low, high, name }`: the track's own (`track.meta.range = { low, high }`), else guessed from the words of its name and its devices' names, else C3 to C6.
- `paw.harmony.scale_names()`: Names of the known scales, sorted.
- `paw.harmony.schedule()`: A while after the project changes the reading is made again, so that `harmony.changed` is heard even when nothing asks.
- `paw.harmony.set_key(spec)`: Set the project's key (one edit), or clear it with nil. Returns the key.
- `paw.harmony.snap(key, pitch, dir)`: The pitch of the key nearest to `pitch`: `dir` "nearest" (the default; halfway between two goes up), "up" or "down". Stays within 0..127.
- `paw.harmony.step(key, pitch, n)`: Move a pitch by `n` scale degrees. A pitch outside the key keeps its distance from the scale note below it.
- `paw.harmony.tones(root, quality)`: The pitch classes of a chord of `quality` on `root`, root first.

## Module paw.harmony.read

- `paw.harmony.read.chords(notes, opts)`: Chords over notes in project beats, from `from` to `to` (the notes' span when nil), in windows of `step` beats (0.5). Each chord: `{ at, length, root, quality, bass, tones }` with pitch classes 0..11.
- `paw.harmony.read.correlate(h, profile, tonic)`: How well a histogram of pitch classes fits a key's profile from `tonic`, from -1 to 1 (Pearson's correlation).
- `paw.harmony.read.fit(w, bass, total, root, q)`: How well the chord `root` `quality` fits weights `w` with `bass` and `total`.
- `paw.harmony.read.keys(notes, bars, chords)`: Keys over notes in project beats, bar by bar: `bars` is a list of bar starts with the end after the last. `chords` (as `chords` gives them), when given, weigh their roots and basses as much again: what the harmony stands on says more about the tonic than a melody's notes. Each key `{ at, length, tonic, mode }` with mode "major" or "minor".

## Module paw.harmony.voice

- `paw.harmony.voice.candidates(tones, opts)`: Every voicing of the chord within the options' range, `{ pitches, style }`.
- `paw.harmony.voice.distance(a, b)`: How far voices move from `a` to `b`: voice by voice when they have as many, else each note to the nearest of the other chord, both ways, halved.
- `paw.harmony.voice.voice(tones, opts)`: The best voicing of `tones` (pitch classes, root first). Options: `low`, `high` (48 and 84), `count` (voices; the tones' number), `style` ("smooth"), `prev` and `next` (pitches of the chords around it, to lead from and into), `bass` (the pitch class that must be lowest), `center` (a pitch to stay near when there is no chord before). Nil when nothing fits the range.

## Module paw.health

- `paw.health.check(names)`: Run the checks named (all when none), each a result of `run`.
- `paw.health.executable(name)`: An executable on the PATH, or at a path: where it is, or nil.
- `paw.health.lines(results)`: Results as lines of text with their styles, for a page.
- `paw.health.names()`: The names of the checks, sorted.
- `paw.health.register(name, fn, opts)`: Register a check under `name`, replacing one of that name. `fn(h)` reports through `h`; `opts.desc` says in a few words what it checks.
- `paw.health.run(name)`: Run one check: `{ name, desc, items }`, each item `{ level, text, advice }`.
- `paw.health.worst(results)`: The worst level among results: "ok", "warn" or "error".

## Module paw.help

- `paw.help.add(path, opts)`: Add a page of help: a Markdown file anywhere. `opts.tag` is its tag and what its headings' tags start with (the file's name by default); `opts.ext` the extension it is about and `opts.dir` where that is, for the note shown while it is not loaded. An extension's README.md and doc/*.md need no adding.

  ```lua
  paw.help.add("/path/to/mine/notes.md", { tag = "mine-notes" })
  ```
- `paw.help.back(n)`: Back along the tags followed (`Ctrl-t`).
- `paw.help.complete(rest)`: What `:help` completes: the tags, ranked as `:help` ranks them.
- `paw.help.ex_name(line)`: The command an Ex line runs: `:%s/a/b/g` runs `s`, `:5,8co 17` `co`.
- `paw.help.excerpt_for_map(map, width, rows)`: The section of help that `for_map` would go to, as at most `rows` lines `{ text, style }` wrapped to `width`, for a pane beside a list of keys. The page's name comes first; nil when there is no help for the key.
- `paw.help.find(topic, limit)`: The tags a topic finds, best first, as Vim's `:help` ranks them: the tag itself, then those that start with it, those that hold it, and those that hold its letters in order. Keys may be written either way: `<C-w>o` finds `Ctrl-w o`.
- `paw.help.follow()`: `Ctrl-]`: follow the link under the cursor, or look up the code or the word there.
- `paw.help.for_command(name)`: The help for a command (what `Ctrl-]` does in the commands picker).
- `paw.help.for_map(map)`: The help for a key mapping: of its keys, else of the command it runs (what `Ctrl-]` does in the keys picker).
- `paw.help.grep(pattern)`: `:helpgrep`: every line of help that holds the words, in the quickfix list.
- `paw.help.index()`: What help knows: `{ sources, tags = name -> { name, source, row, col }, list }`.
- `paw.help.is_help(buf)`: Whether a buffer is a page of help.
- `paw.help.jump(tag)`: Go to a tag: remember where from (for `Ctrl-t` and `Ctrl-o`) and show it.
- `paw.help.keyword()`: `K`: look up the word under the cursor, in help or any text.
- `paw.help.lookup(topic)`: The tag a topic goes to, or nil.
- `paw.help.normalize(path)`: A path with `.` and `..` taken out, made absolute from the working directory.
- `paw.help.open(topic)`: `:help topic`: go to the best tag for it, or say there is none.
- `paw.help.owned(index, topic, exact)`: The tag a topic an extension owns goes to: its place in the owner's pages (where `exact` is not already), else the owner's first page.
- `paw.help.owners(topic)`: The extensions that own what a topic names: the command's (`:name`), or a key's when only extensions map it (a key the core maps is the core's). A list, empty for the core's.
- `paw.help.roots()`: The directories that may be a copy of the source tree, the manual and the bundled extensions in it: `$PAW_HOME` (where an installed program keeps them), the runtime's parent (`--runtime`), the tree a loaded extension is in, and the working directory.
- `paw.help.show(source, row, col)`: Show a page at a row: in the help window, else one split off this one (as Vim's `:help` splits), in a graphical frontend as a docked pane (`gw` pops it out). Returns the window.
- `paw.help.slug(text)`: A heading's words as a tag: `Ex: ranges, :s and :g` is `ex-ranges-s-and-g`.
- `paw.help.sources()`: Every page of help, in order: the contents, the manual, the course, the extensions (each with whether it is loaded) and what was added. A page is `{ path, name, aliases, prefix, ext? }`: `name` is its buffer's (`help://name`), `aliases` its tags (the first is shown on its title), `prefix` what its headings' tags start with.
- `paw.help.tags_of_code(text, first)`: The tags a piece of code names: a command line its command, `:set x` the option too, a Lua name and the modules it is in, an address, an option, a command's name, a key. `first`: it is where something is described (a table's first column), so any short word in it is a tag.
- `paw.help.topic_of(view)`: The topic of help for a view, for the key line: its `help` field, a section of the manual, or the page of the extension it is from.

## Module paw.hooks

- `paw.hooks.key(key)`: Before a key is dispatched: `key.pre` sees it first. False when a handler took it, and the keymap is not to have it.
- `paw.hooks.note(name, payload)`: Count an event delivered this turn towards the turn's edit. Undo, redo and opening a project are not edits (`restored`).
- `paw.hooks.selection()`: What is selected now: the visual selection of the focused view, the clips chosen with the pointer and the chosen notes of the clips the piano roll edits.
- `paw.hooks.turn()`: The end of a turn, after its events are delivered: the kernel's `settle`.
- `paw.hooks.views_shown()`: The names of the views on screen.

## Module paw.keymap

- `paw.keymap.after_next(fn)`: Run `fn` once the next whole command has been typed and done, as insert mode's Ctrl-o goes back to insert mode after one command.
- `paw.keymap.all(view)`: Every mapping that can be typed while `view` has focus, each once: normal mode, then what only a selection, an operator or insert mode takes. Each comes with `kind`: "key", "motion", "operator", "object", "visual" or "insert".
- `paw.keymap.change(n)`: Go to where an earlier edit happened (`n` back, a negative `n` forward again). The first step from the place of the last edit goes to the one before.
- `paw.keymap.changed()`: Note a change that is not an edit of the project (a text buffer's lines), so that `.` repeats the command that made it.
- `paw.keymap.changes(view)`: The places edits happened in a view, oldest first.
- `paw.keymap.classic(lhs, rhs, opts)`: A mapping as it was before the rule: made when `paw.opt.keys` is "classic", now or later, over the mapping the rule gives the same keys, and taken away again when the option changes back. A false `rhs` takes the keys away instead.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.classic("j", "track.volume by=-1", { view = "mixer", desc = "Volume down 1 dB" })
  ```
- `paw.keymap.del(lhs, opts)`: Remove a mapping: `opts.mode` and `opts.view` as `set` took them.
- `paw.keymap.delmarks(spec, all)`: Remove marks from every view, as Vim's `:delmarks` does: `spec` lists letters and ranges (`"a b"`, `"a-d"`), and `all` removes every lowercase one. Returns how many were removed, or nil and what is wrong.
- `paw.keymap.dispatch(key)`: Handle one key as if it were typed. The kernel calls this; scripts use `feed`.
- `paw.keymap.each(fn)`: Call `fn(map, mode, scope, keys)` for every mapping, in no order, `keys` run together as `put` takes them: `every` without the sorting.
- `paw.keymap.escape_hint()`: After an Escape that had nothing to cancel: a second one within two seconds outside the arrange view says how to leave.
- `paw.keymap.every()`: Every mapping in every mode and scope, sorted by scope, mode and keys. What checks the key rules walks (`tests/keys_constitution.lua`).
- `paw.keymap.expand(lhs)`: Write `<leader>` and `<localleader>` as the keys the options name.
- `paw.keymap.feed(keys)`: Type keys as if from the keyboard: `paw.keymap.feed("jj<Space>")`.
- `paw.keymap.getreg(name)`: What a register holds (the unnamed one when `name` is nil).
- `paw.keymap.goto_mark(name)`: Move to a mark; `'` or a backtick as the name goes back to where the last jump came from, and `.` goes to where the last edit was.
- `paw.keymap.group(prefix, name, opts)`: Name a prefix that only leads to more keys, so that the hints after it say `+mixer` where they would say how many keys are behind it.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.group("<leader>x", "mix checks")
  ```

  With `opts.view` the name holds only while that view has focus.
- `paw.keymap.group_name(keys)`: The name given to a prefix with `group`, if any.
- `paw.keymap.groups()`: The names given to prefixes with `group`: scope -> keys -> name.
- `paw.keymap.has(mode, map)`: Whether a mapping is also made, with the same keys and scope, in `mode`.
- `paw.keymap.hints()`: The keys that can follow what has been typed, once the typist has paused: a list of { key, desc }, and a title. Nil when there is nothing to offer.
- `paw.keymap.human(keys)`: Keys as a person writes them: `<A-h>` is `Alt-h`, `<leader>at` is `,at`, `<localleader>d` is `\d`, `<C-w>o` is `Ctrl-w o`, `<CR>` is `Enter`. Takes an lhs or a list of keys.
- `paw.keymap.jump(n)`: Go back (or with a negative `n` forward again) through the places jumped from.
- `paw.keymap.last_selection()`: The last selection made in the focused view, as `'<,'>` names it: the one open now, or the one visual mode last closed. Nil if there is none.
- `paw.keymap.list(mode, view)`: Mappings that apply in `mode` for `view`, the view's own first.
- `paw.keymap.mark(name)`: Set mark `name` (a letter) at the cursor of the focused view.
- `paw.keymap.marks(view)`: The marks of a view: name -> position.
- `paw.keymap.normal(keys)`: Type keys from inside a mapping, the way `:normal` does: they run as part of the command that is running, not as a command of their own.
- `paw.keymap.operator(lhs, fn, opts)`: Define an operator: `fn(region, ctx)` acts on a region of the focused view. A region has `r0`, `r1` (rows, inclusive), `c0`, `c1` (beats, the end not included) and `kind`: "char" for a stretch of time, "line" for whole rows, "block" for a rectangle.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.operator("gl", function(region) ... end, { view = "arrange", desc = "Loop" })
  ```

  With `count = "operator"` the count typed before the operator is its own (how far, how many times: `3gUib` is three steps up over a bar), as `ctx.op_count`, and `ctx.count` is the motion's or object's alone.
- `paw.keymap.parse(lhs)`: Split `gg<C-x>` into { "g", "g", "<C-x>" }, expanding `<leader>` and `<localleader>`.
- `paw.keymap.pending()`: What has been typed towards a command, for display: `"a2d3`.
- `paw.keymap.play(name, n)`: Play the keys in a register `n` times; `@` as the name plays the last one again.
- `paw.keymap.push_jump()`: Remember where the cursor is before it goes somewhere far away.
- `paw.keymap.put(mode, scope, keys, map)`: Put a mapping back as `map` (one `every` gave), or remove it with nil, by its mode, scope and keys run together (`table.concat(map.keys)`): what unloading an extension does with the keys it mapped.
- `paw.keymap.record(name)`: Start recording keys into a register, or stop with no name.
- `paw.keymap.recording()`: The register being recorded into, if any.
- `paw.keymap.repeat_last(n)`: Do the last change again, with `n` in place of its count if given.
- `paw.keymap.scopes()`: Where mappings are looked up, first to last: the part of the focused view the cursor is in, if the view has such parts (`view:subscope()`, such as "arrange.lane" on an automation lane row, or a list of them, first first), the view, then everywhere.
- `paw.keymap.search(text, dir)`: Search the focused view for `text`, forward (`dir` 1) or back (-1).
- `paw.keymap.search_next(dir, n)`: Move to the next (`dir` 1) or previous (-1) thing in the focused view that matches the last search. Views say what matches through `grid.search`.
- `paw.keymap.selection()`: The region selected in the focused view, or nil outside visual mode. From the cursor to where the selection began, both ends included when the view says how far the thing under the cursor reaches (`grid.extent`); a selection that has not been stretched yet covers one grid step. While a command runs with `:'<,'>`, the selection it names.
- `paw.keymap.set(lhs, rhs, opts)`: Map keys.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.set("M", "track.mute", { desc = "Mute track" })
  paw.keymap.set("<leader>x", function(ctx) ... end, { view = "arrange" })
  ```

  `ctx` has `count`, `register` and, for mappings made with `char = true`, the key typed after the mapping as `char`.  Options: `mode` (one or a list, default "n"), `view`, `desc`; `motion = true` for a mapping that only moves the cursor, which makes it work in visual mode and after an operator as well; `linewise = true` for a motion across rows; `jump = true` to remember where the cursor was for `<C-o>`; `repeatable = false` to keep `.` from repeating it.
- `paw.keymap.set_mode(mode)`: Change mode. Leaving visual mode closes the selection; `gv` reopens it.
- `paw.keymap.setreg(value, name, yank)`: Put a value in a register: the unnamed one, and `name` if given. With `yank` and no name it also goes to `"0`, which deleting never touches. A value is a table with a `kind`; what else it holds is up to whoever yanks and pastes it. `"_` discards.
- `paw.keymap.textobject(lhs, fn, opts)`: Define a text object: `fn(ctx)` returns a region, or nil when there is nothing of that kind at the cursor.

  ```lua
  paw.keymap.textobject("ic", function() ... end, { view = "arrange", desc = "The clip" })
  ```
- `paw.keymap.visual_restore()`: Open the last selection again.
- `paw.keymap.visual_start(kind)`: Start selecting from the cursor: "v" a stretch of time, "V" whole rows, "b" a rectangle. The same kind again leaves visual mode.
- `paw.keymap.visual_swap()`: Swap the cursor with the selection's other end.
- `paw.keymap.with_selection(region_, fn, ...)`: Run `fn(...)` with `region` as the selection, the way `:'<,'>` runs a command: anything that asks for the selection meanwhile gets it.

## Module paw.keyrule

- `paw.keyrule.broken()`: Every mapping that breaks the rule, as "scope mode keys: why", sorted. Insert mode is left out (its keys enter material), and so are keys made with `prompt = true`, which answer a question on the screen.
- `paw.keyrule.lost_groups()`: Named groups of keys that lead to no key, as "scope keys (name)".

## Module paw.lanes

- `paw.lanes.any_open()`: Whether any track has its lanes open.
- `paw.lanes.edit(lane_id, fn)`: Change the lane's points with `fn(points)`, which edits the list in place.
- `paw.lanes.format(lane, value)`: A value of a lane as its target shows it: "-6.0 dB", "L30", "800 Hz".
- `paw.lanes.is_open(track)`: Whether a track's lanes are shown as rows.
- `paw.lanes.lines()`: Every row of the arrange view in order: each track drawn, then its lanes when they are open.
- `paw.lanes.name(lane)`: What a lane is called: Volume, Pan, or its device and parameter.
- `paw.lanes.open(track, on)`: Show a track's lanes as rows, or hide them (`on` false).
- `paw.lanes.param_of(lane)`: The parameter a lane moves: its name, and the parameter's description for a device's lane.
- `paw.lanes.point_at(lane_id, beat, reach)`: The point at a beat, within `reach` beats: its index in the lane's points, and the point { beat, value }.
- `paw.lanes.shown(track)`: The lanes shown under a track: none when they are closed.
- `paw.lanes.step(lane)`: How far `+` and `-` move a point: a dB, 5% of pan, one choice, or a hundredth of the parameter's range.
- `paw.lanes.toggle(track)`: Show a track's automation lanes, or hide them; returns whether they show.
- `paw.lanes.value_at(lane, beat)`: What a lane's target is at a beat: the curve's value, or with no points yet the target's own value.

## Module paw.launcher

- `paw.launcher.back(track)`: Send a track back to its timeline; with no track, every track that left it.
- `paw.launcher.boundary(beat, q)`: The first boundary of a quantize (the project's by default) at or after `beat`, as the engine finds it.
- `paw.launcher.capture(on)`: Start or stop capturing. Stopping while the song plays writes what has been captured so far.
- `paw.launcher.clip(track, row)`: The clip in a slot, or nil.
- `paw.launcher.copy(clip, track, row)`: Copy a clip from the timeline (or another slot) into a slot.
- `paw.launcher.finish_recording()`: End the clip being recorded into a slot.
- `paw.launcher.launch(track, row, opts)`: Launch the clip in a slot on its next boundary; an empty slot stops the track. `opts.quantize` and `opts.legato` stand in for the slot's.
- `paw.launcher.new_clip(track, row, bars)`: An empty MIDI clip of `bars` bars (1) in a slot. Returns its id.
- `paw.launcher.playing(track)`: What one track plays: "arrangement", "stopped" or a row; and what it has queued, if anything.
- `paw.launcher.press(track, row)`: A slot's button pressed, from a key, the mouse or a controller: what that does is the clip's mode. A toggle stops a clip that plays or is queued.
- `paw.launcher.record(track, row, bars)`: Record `bars` bars (1) into an empty slot of a track, from the next boundary of the project's quantize. The track is armed if it is not, and stops what it plays at that boundary. Starts the song if it is stopped; stopping it early keeps what was recorded.
- `paw.launcher.release(track, row)`: A slot's button let go: a gate clip stops.
- `paw.launcher.rows()`: How many rows there are: those with clips or names, one empty row more, and at least `paw.opt.launch_rows`.
- `paw.launcher.scene(row)`: Launch a scene: the clip in that row on every track that has one, all on the same boundary. Tracks without one stop what they play from a slot.
- `paw.launcher.scene_name(row)`: A scene's name (rows from 0): its own, or "Scene N".
- `paw.launcher.scenes()`: The names of the scenes, by row from 1; rows without one are nil.
- `paw.launcher.set_quantize(q)`: Where launches land unless a slot says otherwise.
- `paw.launcher.set_scene_name(row, name)`: Name a scene (rows from 0), kept with the project.
- `paw.launcher.slots(track)`: The clips in a track's slots, by row: `{ [row] = clip view }`.
- `paw.launcher.state()`: What each track plays and has queued, by track id: see `paw.api.launcher`. A track with nothing launched is missing.
- `paw.launcher.stop(track)`: Stop a track's clip on the next boundary; with no track, every track's. A stopped track is silent until it is launched again or sent back.
- `paw.launcher.write_captured(position)`: Write what has been captured and not written yet, up to `position` where it is still under way, as one undo step.

## Module paw.layout

- `paw.layout.all_windows()`: Every window of every tab, as `{ win, tab }`.
- `paw.layout.alternate(win)`: Show again what a window (the current one) showed before what it shows now: Vim's alternate buffer, `Ctrl-^` and `:b#`.
- `paw.layout.border_at(rects, x, y)`: The border between two windows at a cell of an arrangement (`paw.ui.arrange`): the rule between windows side by side, or the top row of a window below another.
- `paw.layout.buf_create(type_name, target)`: A buffer of a type for a target, made if there is none. A view's type has one buffer, whatever the target.
- `paw.layout.buf_delete(buf)`: Delete a buffer (`:bd`): its windows close, and a buffer of a type that has more than one is forgotten. A view's buffer stays, as the view does.
- `paw.layout.buf_of(win)`: The buffer a window shows.
- `paw.layout.buffer_names()`: Names to complete after `:b`, `:e`, `:sp`, `:vs`: every buffer's and every view's that can be shown.
- `paw.layout.buffers_list()`: The buffers to list (`:ls`), by number: the views' that are in the layout or docked, and every other made since and not deleted.
- `paw.layout.buftype`: the same as `paw.buftype`.
- `paw.layout.capture()`: The tabs and windows as plain data: what `:layout save` writes.
- `paw.layout.close(win)`: Close a window: a view's keeps its place, hidden; any other goes. The last window of a tab closes the tab; the last of all does not close. Returns whether it closed.
- `paw.layout.conceal(name)`: Hide a view's windows in every tab. Returns whether one was on screen.
- `paw.layout.current()`: The window the keyboard is in, in the current tab: the last one entered, or the window of the focused view when focus was given by its name.
- `paw.layout.default_tree()`: The tree every tab starts with: the arrange view, and the panels' places, closed.
- `paw.layout.dock(name, opts)`: Dock a view in the current tab and remember the place for other tabs. See `paw.ui.dock`.
- `paw.layout.drag_border(border, rects, x, y)`: Move a border to where the pointer is: the one of the two sides that has a size of its own keeps one, else the first side gets one.
- `paw.layout.drop_dead()`: Close the windows of buffers whose target is gone, as when another project is opened (a window with `paw://lane/9` in it): a type says so with `alive(buf)`. A window that cannot close, the last one, is left empty.
- `paw.layout.enter(win)`: Make a window the current one and give it the keyboard.
- `paw.layout.equalize()`: Give every window of the current tab an equal share, but strips that do not take the keyboard.
- `paw.layout.exchange(count)`: Exchange the current window with the next one beside it (the one before, when it is the last), or the `count`th, within their row or column; the next may be a split of several.
- `paw.layout.export(node)`: A tree of windows as plain data, for `paw.layouts` and saving.
- `paw.layout.find(root, name)`: The window of a view in a tree, one on screen first.
- `paw.layout.find_id(root, id)`: The window of an id in the tree under `root`.
- `paw.layout.focusable_windows()`: The windows of the current tab that take the keyboard.
- `paw.layout.get(id)`: A window by its number, and the tab it is in.
- `paw.layout.import(spec)`: A node as saved, or as a configuration writes it: `"roll"` or `{ view = "roll", size = 20 }` for a window, `{ dir = "h", "arrange", "roll" }` (or with `children`) for a split. Windows of views that are not there (an extension not loaded) are left out.
- `paw.layout.layout_names()`: The names of the layouts there are: the configuration's and those saved.
- `paw.layout.leaf(view, fields)`: A new window showing `view`, with fields such as `size` or `hidden`.
- `paw.layout.load(name)`: Put back layout `name`: the configuration's, else one saved.
- `paw.layout.maximize()`: Give the current window the whole tab, or put the others back.
- `paw.layout.move_to_edge(edge)`: Move the current window to an edge of the tab ("H", "J", "K", "L"), the whole height or width of it.
- `paw.layout.neighbour(dir, count)`: The window next to the current one in a direction ("h", "j", "k", "l"), `count` steps on.
- `paw.layout.only(win)`: Close every window of the current tab but one.
- `paw.layout.parent_of(node, target)`: The split holding `target` in the tree under `node`, and its place there.
- `paw.layout.powers(scope, def, wrap)`: Map what `def` declares in key scope `scope` (a view's name, or a part of one: see `paw.keymap.scopes`), so that a buffer type or a kind of text buffer says its keys where it is made:

  ```lua
  keymaps     = { ["<localleader>r"] = fn or "command line" or { fn, desc = "...", mode = ... } }
  motions     = { ["]p"] = fn }      -- also after operators and in visual mode
  textobjects = { ip = fn }          -- fn(ctx) returns a region
  operators   = { gq = fn }          -- fn(region, ctx)
  ```

  `wrap(fn)`, if given, makes each function what the keymap calls, to add to its `ctx` (the first argument).
- `paw.layout.resize(win, axis, n, relative)`: Resize a window (the current one): `axis` "height" or "width", to `n` cells, or by `n` with `relative`. It is the window's row or column in the split along that axis that changes. Returns false when nothing can.
- `paw.layout.resolve(name)`: The type and buffer a name stands for: a buffer's name or number, a view's name or short name (`roll`), or a type with a target (`type://target`). Nil when it names nothing.
- `paw.layout.restore(saved)`: Put back tabs and windows from `M.capture()`'s data, or from a list of tabs as a configuration writes them:

  ```lua
  { { name = "Edit", layout = { dir = "h", "arrange", "roll" } }, { name = "Mix", layout = "mixer" } }
  ```

  Returns false when it holds no window.
- `paw.layout.reveal(name, go)`: Put a view's window on screen in the current tab: where it was, else where it docked. With `go`, a view on screen in another tab is gone to instead. Returns the window, or nil for a view that has no place (one that floats).
- `paw.layout.rotate(back)`: Rotate the windows of the current window's row or column: each moves one place on (`back`: one place back).
- `paw.layout.save(name)`: Write the tabs and windows as layout `name`, in the state directory.
- `paw.layout.set_option(win, name, value)`: Set a window option (`timebind`) on a window (the current one).
- `paw.layout.set_size(node, axis, size)`: Set the size a node takes along its parent: a panel whose size is an option (`devices_width`) has it set there.
- `paw.layout.setup()`: Make the empty buffer type, the commands and the keys. Run once the default commands are there, as some of these take over their short names.
- `paw.layout.show_in(win, name, buf)`: Show a buffer in a window instead of the one it shows. A view on screen in another window moves here.
- `paw.layout.shown(node)`: Whether a node takes room: a window that is not hidden, or a node with one.
- `paw.layout.split(opts)`: Split a window (the current one) and show a buffer in the new half, which gets the keyboard. `opts`: `vertical` (side by side), `view` (the type; "empty" by default), `buf` (a buffer of a type that has more than one), `win`. Returns the new window, or nil and why not.
- `paw.layout.tab()`: The current tab.
- `paw.layout.tab_close(i)`: Close tab `i` (the current one); the last tab does not close.
- `paw.layout.tab_copy(name)`: Make a tab with the same windows as the current one, after it, and go to it, the keyboard in the same kind of window. Views shown in a window of each show the same state in both.
- `paw.layout.tab_go(i)`: Go to tab `i`.
- `paw.layout.tab_new(name, view, win)`: Make a tab, after the current one, and go to it. It shows a buffer (a view's name, or `buf`) or the window `win`; an empty window without.
- `paw.layout.tab_step(n)`: Go `n` tabs on (back, when negative), round the end.
- `paw.layout.tab_title(t)`: What a tab is called: its name, else the buffer of its current window.
- `paw.layout.tidy(root)`: Merge splits of one child and splits the same way as their parent.
- `paw.layout.time_follow(lead, win)`: After the leading window is drawn: the others take its time.
- `paw.layout.time_lead()`: Before the windows are drawn: the current window, if it is time bound, leads the others that are. Returns the window to draw first and the set of windows that follow it.
- `paw.layout.title(buf)`: What a buffer is called on screen.
- `paw.layout.to_tab()`: Move the current window to a tab of its own.
- `paw.layout.windows(root, all)`: The windows of a tree in order, the hidden ones too with `all`. A window made by code that only gave it a view gets what a window has.

## Module paw.learn

- `paw.learn.bind(source, target)`: Bind a controller to a target, in place of whatever moved that target before. `source` is { cc = 74 }, { bend = true } or { pressure = true }, or for a button { note = 36 }, with `channel` (1 to 16) or without for any channel. Returns the binding.
- `paw.learn.bindings()`: The bindings: { { source, channel, number, track, target, device, param }, ... }.
- `paw.learn.bound(target)`: What moves a target: its binding, or nil.
- `paw.learn.cancel()`: Stop waiting for a controller to learn.
- `paw.learn.clear()`: Forget every controller binding.
- `paw.learn.is_trigger(target)`: Whether a target is pressed rather than moved.
- `paw.learn.source(event)`: The source of a `midi.in` event that can move something, or nil: { source, number, channel, value } with the value from 0 to 1.
- `paw.learn.source_name(b)`: A controller as text: "CC 74 ch 1", "pitch wheel ch 2", "note 36 ch 10".
- `paw.learn.start(target)`: Wait for the next controller move and bind it to `target` (or to what was moved last).
- `paw.learn.target_for(word)`: The target a word names on the selected track: "volume", "pan", or a parameter of one of its devices by key or name.
- `paw.learn.target_name(t)`: What a binding moves, as text: "Lead › volume", "Lead › Filter › Cutoff".
- `paw.learn.unbind(which)`: Take a binding away: by its place in `bindings()`, or everything that moves a target. Returns how many went.
- `paw.learn.under_cursor()`: What the keyboard is on, if that is something a controller can move: the parameter under the device panel's cursor, the mixer's fader.

## Module paw.limit

- `paw.limit.call(name, fn, ...)`: Call `fn(...)` with the time limit as `guard` does, but give its error to the caller instead of reporting it: for a call whose caller is told what went wrong, such as a request on the control socket.
- `paw.limit.extend(ms)`: Give the running call more time, as `:lua` does: `ms` from now.
- `paw.limit.guard(name, fn, ...)`: Call `fn(...)` under the time limit for Lua (`paw.opt.lua_limit`): a call that runs too long is stopped and reported as `name`; errors are reported, not raised. Returns what `fn` returned.
- `paw.limit.named(name, fn, ...)`: Name what runs inside the limited call, for the error should it run away: `paw.limit.named("command `x`", fn, ...)`.
- `paw.limit.unhurried(fn, ...)`: Run `fn(...)` with its time not counted, for work that is known to be long and to end: `paw.limit.unhurried(synthesise, phrase)`. Callbacks the kernel makes meanwhile (timers during a wait) get a limit of their own.
- `paw.limit.untrusted(fn)`: Mark a function that is not the runtime's own. Where the limit reaches into compiled code this does nothing. Where it does not, the function and every function made inside it are kept out of the JIT compiler, so that the limit can stop their loops (unless the limit is turned off with `paw.opt.lua_limit = 0` before the code is loaded).

## Module paw.loading

- `paw.loading.memory(path)`: What is remembered of a project's plugins: `stopped` maps device ids (as strings) to `{ kind, name, reason }`.
- `paw.loading.offline()`: Set every plugin offline. Returns how many.
- `paw.loading.online()`: Bring every offline device up. Returns how many.
- `paw.loading.open(path, opts)`: Open a project, offline as `opts` says (`plugins_offline`, or `offline`, a list of device ids), and with the devices that could not be loaded last time offline as well.
- `paw.loading.project_dir(path)`: The directory the program keeps things about a project in, outside the project file: one per project file.
- `paw.loading.suggested(path)`: The devices of the project at `path` that could not be loaded last time, as a list of `{ id, kind, name, reason }`.
- `paw.loading.toggle(device)`: Set one device offline, or back online.

## Module paw.lsp

- `paw.lsp.actions_at(location, cb)`: Ask every server that offers actions, and holds the location, what can be done there; `cb(actions)` gets `{ { title, source, edit | run } }`.
- `paw.lsp.adapter(name, spec)`: Add a dialect: how a kind of server is spoken to (see paw/lsp/standard.lua for the functions an adapter has; any it leaves out are the standard ones).
- `paw.lsp.attach(which, address, keep, subject)`: Have a server keep a subject of an address open whether or not it would be sent otherwise (`keep` false lets it go). A clip id names its clip.
- `paw.lsp.attaches(which, address, subject)`: Whether a server is attached to an address (for its subject, or any).
- `paw.lsp.cancel(which, id)`: Tell a server to forget a request it has not answered yet.
- `paw.lsp.clients()`: The servers that were enabled, as `{ name, status, error, transport, subjects, capabilities, server, pid, documents, client }`.
- `paw.lsp.code_actions(location)`: Pick a fix or an action for a location (by default what is under the cursor of the focused view; off a note in the piano roll, the diagnostics where the cursor is), and carry it out as one undo step.
- `paw.lsp.command(ctx)`: `:lsp [info|start|stop|restart|log] [name]`.
- `paw.lsp.command_complete()`: What `:Lsp` completes to: its words and the configured servers.
- `paw.lsp.complete(ctx, done)`: A completion source over every running server that suggests, in the shape `paw.complete.register` takes: `ctx` names the `clip` and where the suggestion starts (`at`, beats from the clip's start), with an optional `selection` (a note set of the clip) and `controller`. `done(items)` is called once.
- `paw.lsp.complete_cancel()`: Forget the completion requests still out (a newer one replaced them).
- `paw.lsp.config(name, config)`: Say how to start a server and what to show it, as `vim.lsp.config`. A second call changes only the fields it gives.

  ```lua
  cmd          the program and its arguments (or a function giving them)
  server       instead: a Lua table of handlers, run in this process
  kind         "oneshot": `cmd` is run once per version of each subject
               (placeholders `{file}`, `{input}`, `{uri}` and the settings),
               with `timeout_ms`, `accepts(doc)` (whether to run on it),
               `input(doc)` (what it is given, the subject by default)
               and `diagnostic(finding, doc)` (a location, fixes)
  framing      "lines" (newline-delimited JSON, the default) or "headers" (Content-Length)
  adapter      the dialect, by name or as a table (LSP's own by default)
  attach       { subjects = { "clip", "mix", ... }, where = { focus, tracks = { "Flute*" }, drums } }
  settings     sent at initialize and with `workspace/didChangeConfiguration`
  init_options sent once, as `initializationOptions`
  restart      { max = 3, within_s = 60 }: restarts after it dies (none by default)
  env, cwd     for the process
  ```
- `paw.lsp.document(which, uri)`: The document a server holds under a URI, or nil.
- `paw.lsp.enable(name, on)`: Start a configured server (`on` false stops it).
- `paw.lsp.has(which, feature, lane)`: Whether a running server (a client or its name) offers a feature: "hover", "completion", "actions", "diagnostics", "analysis".
- `paw.lsp.hover(id, pitch, beat, cb)`: Ask about a place in a clip (`pitch` and `beat` from its start), as before addresses: the same as `hover_at` on the note there.
- `paw.lsp.hover_at(location, cb)`: Ask every server that hovers, and holds the location, what it says there; `cb(sections)` gets `{ { client, lines } }` once all have answered.
- `paw.lsp.info_lines()`: What `:lsp info` shows: each server, its transport, state, what it is attached to and can do, and what it holds.
- `paw.lsp.log_path(name)`: Where a server's errors are written.
- `paw.lsp.notify(which, method, params)`: Tell a server something that has no answer.
- `paw.lsp.request(which, method, params, cb)`: Ask a server something; `cb(err, result)` is called with its answer. Returns the request's id, or nil when the server is not there.
- `paw.lsp.restart(name)`: Stop a server and start it again.
- `paw.lsp.settle(ms)`: Wait in a script until every server has started and answered what it was sent, and every one-shot run has finished (or `ms` have passed, 10 s by default). Returns whether they did.
- `paw.lsp.show_hover(id, pitch, beat)`: Show what is known about a location (by default what is under the cursor of the focused view): the diagnostics about it and what it holds, then each server's hover, in a float.
- `paw.lsp.show_lines(location, lines, sections)`: The hover float itself: the diagnostics' lines, then each server's.
- `paw.lsp.stop(name)`: Stop every server, or the one named.
- `paw.lsp.subject(name, spec)`: Add a subject (see paw/lsp/subjects.lua).
- `paw.lsp.sync()`: Bring every server up to date now: open what it is attached to, send what changed, close what it no longer is. Requests call this first, so that they are about what is there.

## Module paw.lsp.document_module

- `paw.lsp.document_module.beats(ticks)`: Beats from the clip's start for a tick of its document.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.build(id, hash)`: The document for a clip, as `midi/didOpen` and `midi/didChange` send it, under `hash` (from `key_of`). Nil when the clip is gone.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.clip_of(uri)`: The clip a URI names, or nil.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.is_drums(track)`: Whether a track plays drums: a drum map on it (extensions/drums keeps one in `meta.drums`), or a name such as "Drums", "Kit" or "Perc".
- `paw.lsp.document_module.key(beat)`: The project's key at a beat as `{ root = 0..11, scale = "major" }`: from `paw.harmony` when there is one, else the key extensions/musicops keeps in the project. Nil when nobody has said.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.key_of(id)`: Something that changes whenever what would be sent about a clip does, and is cheap to make: its notes, where it is, the tracks around it, the tempo map and the key. Nil when the clip is gone.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.tick(beats)`: Beats as ticks of `M.PPQ` a beat, the language server's unit.
- `paw.lsp.document_module.uri(id)`: The URI that names a clip: `paw://clip/12`.

## Module paw.luadev

- `paw.luadev.add_dir(dir, rank)`: Look for devices in `dir` too. `rank` (default `M.RANK_EXTENSION`) says whose script wins where two directories have one of the same name.
- `paw.luadev.check()`: Look at every script again: those that changed are loaded, and the devices made from them start again with the parameters they had. Returns what `paw.api.lua_devices_rescan` found.
- `paw.luadev.watch()`: Look at the scripts' files every `paw.opt.lua_devices_watch` ms (0 for never). Started by itself once a directory is added.

## Module paw.markdown

- `paw.markdown.inline(s, style, link, out)`: The runs of a line of Markdown, each with the style and link given.
- `paw.markdown.parse(text)`: Markdown as a list of blocks (headings, paragraphs, lists, code, tables) for `render`.
- `paw.markdown.plain(s)`: The text of runs without their marks: a heading as it reads.
- `paw.markdown.render(blocks, opts)`: The blocks as lines `opts.width` wide (78 by default). `opts.heading_tag(block)` gives the tag shown at the right of a heading (as Vim's help shows `*tag*`). Returns `{ lines, anchors }`; an anchor is `{ row, kind = "heading" | "tags" | "code" | "lead", ... }` ("lead": the bold words a paragraph starts with).
- `paw.markdown.width(s)`: How many cells a string takes.

## Module paw.markers

- `paw.markers.add(beat, name, opts)`: Add a marker at a beat; with `opts.length` a region from there. Returns it.
- `paw.markers.at(beat, reach)`: The marker or region start nearest a beat within `reach` beats (half a grid step by default), or the region the beat is inside.
- `paw.markers.find(which)`: The marker or region a number (its place in the song), an id given as `{ id = n }`, or a name means; nil without one.
- `paw.markers.label(marker)`: What a marker is called on screen: its name, or its number in the song.
- `paw.markers.list()`: Every marker and region, in order of time: { id, beat, name, length, color }. A region has a `length` in beats; a marker has none.
- `paw.markers.next(beat)`: The first marker after a beat, and the last before it.
- `paw.markers.prev(beat)`: The last marker before a beat, or nil.
- `paw.markers.region(which)`: A region by number, id or name.
- `paw.markers.regions()`: The regions alone.
- `paw.markers.remove(id)`: Remove a marker by id.
- `paw.markers.render_regions(dir, opts)`: Render every region to a file of its own in `dir`, named after it: `01 Intro.wav`. `opts` is as for `paw.render`, plus `format` ("wav", "flac", "mp3", "ogg" or "opus"). Returns the files.
- `paw.markers.set(id, fields)`: Change a marker: `fields` may hold beat, name, length (false makes a region a marker again) and color.

## Module paw.media

- `paw.media.collect()`: Copy every file from outside the project's folder into `media` beside it and point the clips at the copies. One undo step. Returns `{ copied, missing, dir }`.
- `paw.media.glue(clips)`: Join audio clips of one track into one clip playing a new file: the clips given, or with one, it and every audio clip touching or overlapping it. Returns { id, file, glued }.
- `paw.media.list()`: Every file the project plays: `{ path, missing, inside }`.
- `paw.media.missing()`: Files the project's clips play that are not there, once each.
- `paw.media.normalize(clip, level)`: Bring the loudest sample an audio clip plays to `level` dB (0) by its gain. Returns the new gain.
- `paw.media.relink(from, to)`: Point the clips that play `from` at the file `to`, and look beside it for the other missing files. One undo step. Returns `{ clips, found, missing }`.
- `paw.media.relink_pick()`: Choose a file for a missing one, or a directory to search for them all.
- `paw.media.reverse(clip)`: Play an audio clip backwards, from a new reversed copy of its part of the file.
- `paw.media.search(dir)`: Look for every missing file in a directory tree. One undo step. Returns `{ found, missing }`.

## Module paw.midifile

- `paw.midifile.encode(file)`: Bytes of a Standard MIDI File from the shape `parse` returns (`format` 0 or 1, `ppq`, `tracks`, and `tempos`, `signatures`, `markers`, which go in the first track). Ticks may be fractions; they are rounded.
- `paw.midifile.export(path, opts)`: Write a format 1 MIDI file with the tempo map, time signatures and markers: of the whole project, of `opts.tracks` (tracks or ids), or of `opts.clips` (ids) alone. Returns how many notes went in.
- `paw.midifile.import(path, opts)`: Bring a MIDI file into the project: its parts on new tracks below the cursor's, at the cursor (or `opts.start`); with `opts.track`, all of it as one clip on that track instead. The tempo map is left alone unless `opts.tempo`, which puts the file's from where it starts on, and its markers are added. Returns { tracks, clips, notes, skipped }.
- `paw.midifile.is_midi_file(path)`: Whether a path names a MIDI file, by its ending.
- `paw.midifile.open(path)`: Open a MIDI file as a new project with no file of its own (see the top of this file). Returns { tracks, notes, skipped }; errors when the file cannot be read, leaving the open project alone.
- `paw.midifile.parse(data)`: Read the bytes of a Standard MIDI File. Returns, in ticks (`ppq` to a beat) from the start: 

  ```lua
  { format, ppq, length,
    tracks = { { name, instrument, length,
                 notes = { { tick, length, pitch, velocity, channel, lyric, attr } },
                 controls = { { tick, type, value, channel, number, key, program } } } },
    tempos = { { tick, bpm } }, signatures = { { tick, num, den } },
    markers = { { tick, text } }, skipped = { [what] = count } }
  ```

   Channels count from 0. A control's `type` is "cc" (with `number`), "bend" (0 to 16383, 8192 in the middle), "pressure" (with `key` for a single note's) or "program" (with `program`); values are as in the file. Format 2 files (independent patterns) are read as one track after another. A file timed in frames of SMPTE time code is read as if at 120 beats a minute, which is what its seconds are then. Returns nil and a reason when it is not a MIDI file.
- `paw.midifile.parts(file, merge)`: What goes on one track: { name, channel, drums, notes, controls }, in ticks. A format 0 file's one track is split by channel; any other track with notes is one part. With `merge`, everything is one part.
- `paw.midifile.read(path)`: Read a MIDI file from disk: as `parse`, or nil and a reason.
- `paw.midifile.skipped_text(file)`: What was left out of a file, as one line, or nil.

## Module paw.mixer_rows

- `paw.mixer_rows.current()`: The row under the cursor, and the track it is on.
- `paw.mixer_rows.describe_row(id, row)`: What a row is called and holds, for the title bar and `K`.
- `paw.mixer_rows.device()`: The insert under the cursor, for `ge`.
- `paw.mixer_rows.rows(id)`: The rows of a track's strip, top to bottom: { key, kind, index }.
- `paw.mixer_rows.to(i)`: Put the cursor on row `i` (1 for the top) of the cursor track's strip.
- `paw.mixer_rows.to_kind(dir, n)`: Go to the first row of the next (`dir` 1) or previous kind.
- `paw.mixer_rows.to_kind_end(n)`: Move the mixer's cursor to the last row of its kind (or `n` kinds on).

## Module paw.mouse

- `paw.mouse.beat(x, scroll, zoom)`: The beat at the left edge of column `x` of a timeline whose column 0 is beat `scroll`, at `zoom` columns a beat.
- `paw.mouse.done(event)`: Called by `paw.ui.mouse` last: a move over nothing that says what it is under the pointer clears what the status line said.
- `paw.mouse.forget()`: Forget the last press and any gesture under way: the next press is not the second of a double click.
- `paw.mouse.gesture()`: The gesture under way, if any: what was handed to `grab`.
- `paw.mouse.grab(down, handlers)`: Hold the pointer from a press (`down`, as the view got it) until its button is let go: every drag goes to `handlers.drag(e)` and the release to `handlers.up(e)`, wherever the pointer is, with `x` and `y` relative to the view the press was in, `dx` and `dy` the cells from the press, and `moved` whether it has left the cell it went down on. A press of another button meanwhile calls `handlers.cancel()` and ends the gesture.
- `paw.mouse.has(event, letter)`: Whether the modifiers of an event hold `letter` ("C", "A" or "S").
- `paw.mouse.hint(text)`: Say what is under the pointer, or what it would do, on the status line; nil says nothing. A view calls it as the pointer moves over it.
- `paw.mouse.hint_text()`: What the status line says about the pointer, if anything.
- `paw.mouse.mark_double(event)`: Whether a press is the second of a double click: the same button on the same cell soon after the first, which was not itself a second. A window's pointer, in fractions of a cell, counts by the cell it is in.
- `paw.mouse.mode(event)`: How a click with modifiers chooses: "toggle" with Ctrl, "add" with Shift, else "only".
- `paw.mouse.on_grid(x, scroll, zoom, grid)`: The same, on the grid: the step the column's left edge falls in, which is the one drawn there.
- `paw.mouse.take(event)`: Called by `paw.ui.mouse` first: true when the event was taken here and goes no further.
- `paw.mouse.to_surface(target, event)`: Called by `paw.ui.mouse` for the view an event goes to: over the pixels the view shows (`buf:surface`), the event goes to the view's `pointer` as a window gives it (`paw.canvas`), in pixels of its drawing: where the terminal reports the pointer in pixels, exactly; elsewhere at the middle of the cell. `kind` is "down", "up", "move" (a button held), "hover", "double" (after the second press) or "wheel" (`dx`, `dy`); the modifiers are `ctrl`, `shift` and `alt`; `col`, `row` are the screen cell under the pointer, where a menu opens. A drag and its release go to the surface the press was on, wherever the pointer has gone. True when the event went there.
- `paw.mouse.to_view(view, event)`: Give an event in a view's own cells to the view, for a view drawn in a window of its own (`paw.canvas.pointer`): a gesture under way has it first, as in the terminal.
- `paw.mouse.wheel(event)`: A wheel event as a step: 1 down or right, -1 up or left, and whether it goes sideways.

## Module paw.music

- `paw.music.degree(root, scale, degree)`: Pitch of scale degree `degree` (1 is the root, 8 the octave above).
- `paw.music.is_black(pitch)`: Whether a MIDI pitch is a black key.
- `paw.music.name(pitch)`: Name of a MIDI note number: 60 -> "C4".
- `paw.music.pitch(note)`: MIDI note number for a name such as "C4", "f#3" or "Bb2". Numbers pass through.

## Module paw.option

- `paw.option.check(name, value)`: Whether `value` is one that option `name` takes: true, or nil and an error that says what it takes. An option with no default takes anything.
- `paw.option.define(name, default, spec)`: Give an option a default, for extensions that add options of their own. It then takes values of the default's type; `spec` says more:

  ```lua
  paw.option.define("lanes", 4, { min = 1, max = 16, integer = true })
  paw.option.define("look", "plain", { values = { "plain", "fancy" } })
  paw.option.define("size", "auto", { type = { "number", "string" }, min = 1, values = { "auto" } })
  ```
- `paw.option.list()`: Every option that has a default, by name: { name, default }.
- `paw.option.read(name, text)`: The value typed text stands for in option `name` (`true`, `off`, a number, or the text), or nil and an error that says what it takes. A value that is not text is checked as it is.

## Module paw.panes

- `paw.panes.area(width, height)`: The main area's size in pixels, from the frontend: once at the start and whenever it changes. The first time a seat's window says it, the device panel is shown: a window has the selected track's devices beside the timeline unless they are closed.
- `paw.panes.border(index, x, y)`: A border of the last arrangement (by its place in `state().borders`) dragged to `x, y`: the side that has a size keeps one, in whole cells.
- `paw.panes.cells()`: The main area in cells, with the status line and the command line under it as on a terminal: what the seat's screen is. Nil until the frontend has said.
- `paw.panes.close(id)`: Close a pane's window, as `:close` in it would.
- `paw.panes.focus(id)`: Give a pane's window the keyboard, as a click in it does.
- `paw.panes.pointer(id, event, drawn)`: A pointer event in a pane, in pixels from its corner (as `paw.canvas.pointer` takes them): a press gives it the keyboard first. `drawn`, for a pane drawn in cells, says how: its `cell` and its size in them, `cols` and `rows`; it keeps the button held in a drag.
- `paw.panes.state()`: Where everything goes in the main area, for a frontend's state: `panes`, each `{ win, view, kind ("native", "paint", "cells"), title, x, y, w, h, focused }`; `borders`, each `{ dir ("h": a rule between panes side by side, "v": one between panes one above another), x, y, length }`, by their place in the list; `tabs`, each `{ title }`, and `tab`, the current one; `top`, where the panes start under the row of tabs. Nil until the frontend has said how big its area is.
- `paw.panes.tab(i)`: A click on tab `i` goes to it.

## Module paw.params

- `paw.params.apply(device, name)`: Set a device to one of its kind's presets, by name. The same as loading it with `paw.fx.load` (`:preset`): one undo step, and the device then holds that preset.
- `paw.params.format(p, value)`: The value as text, in the parameter's unit.
- `paw.params.fraction(p, value)`: Where the value sits on a slider, 0 to 1.
- `paw.params.from_fraction(p, fraction)`: The value at a slider position, 0 to 1.
- `paw.params.is_log(p)`: Whether the parameter moves on a log scale.
- `paw.params.preset_value(p, value)`: A preset's value for a parameter as a number: a choice may be named.
- `paw.params.presets(kind)`: The built-in presets of a device kind: a list of `{ name, params }`.
- `paw.params.read(device, method, data)`: Ask a built-in device for a reading: a list of numbers (`curve`, `spectrum`) or a table of named numbers (`meters`, `pitch`).
- `paw.params.step(p, value, steps)`: The value `steps` key presses away: a hundredth of the slider each, one option at a time for a choice.

## Module paw.pick

- `paw.pick.file(opts)`: Choose a file by walking directories: 

  ```lua
  paw.pick.file({ title = "Import audio", extensions = { "wav", "mp3" },
                  on_choose = function(path) end })
  ```

   Directories come first and are entered with Enter; `..` goes up; only files with one of `extensions` are listed (all files without it). It starts in `dir`, else where a file was last chosen, else beside the project, else in the home directory. With `directory = true` the first item chooses the directory being shown, and `on_choose` gets it.
- `paw.pick.filter(query, items, format, primary, mode)`: The items that match `query`, best first, each as { item, text, score }; `mode` as `paw.pick.match` takes it.

  ```lua
  paw.pick.filter("bass", { "Bass", "Bass Synth", "Drums" })
  ```
- `paw.pick.hear_file(path)`: Hear a file in a picker of files: a sound file on its own, the first bars of a MIDI file through an instrument. The label for the pane.
- `paw.pick.match(query, text, want_positions, mode)`: How well `query` matches `text`: a score, higher is better, and the byte positions of the matched characters in order. Nil when it does not match. Words of the query separated by spaces must each match. `mode` is one of `paw.pick.MODES`, "fuzzy" by default.

  ```lua
  paw.pick.match("bs", "Bass Synth")   --> score, { 1, 6 }
  ```
- `paw.pick.open(spec, extra)`: Open a picker. See the top of this file for the fields of `spec`, or pass the name of a source. Returns the picker's state.
- `paw.pick.resume()`: Open the last picker again, as it was: what was typed, the mode, the line selected. Its items are read again.
- `paw.pick.show(loc, how)`: Show a location: in place (`how` nil), or in a new window beside ("vsplit"), below ("split") or in a new tab ("tab"), the view that shows it best moving there. Returns whether there was somewhere to go.
- `paw.pick.state()`: The open picker, if any: its query, the matches as lines, and the item under the selection. For tests and for frontends.

## Module paw.plot

- `paw.plot.alpha(colour, alpha)`: A colour `#rrggbb` at `alpha` (0 to 1), as `#rrggbbaa`.
- `paw.plot.bars(g, px, opts)`: Bars over time in a strip, one for each of `opts.items`, `{ beat, value, color, bright }` (`value` from 0 at the bottom to 1 at the top, `bright` for one that is chosen), each `opts.width` pixels wide (3) from the bottom, with a head. `from` and `pixels_per_beat` as for `M.curve`; `color` for the bars that have none of their own.
- `paw.plot.bars_cells(buf, opts)`: `M.bars` in cells: a column of eighth blocks for each item.
- `paw.plot.curve(g, px, opts)`: Draw a curve over time in a strip: its grid, the area under it, the line, and its points. `px` is the strip's size as `buf:strip` gives it (`w`, `h`, `cell`). `opts`:

  ```lua
  points            `{ beat, value, shape, tension }` each, in order, as `paw.curves` has them
  from              the beat at the left edge
  pixels_per_beat   the zoom
  frac              `frac(value)` from 0 (bottom) to 1 (top); else `lo` and `hi`
  flat              the value shown when there are no points (else nothing is)
  color             the line's colour, `#rrggbb` (the theme's `dim` by default):
                    a track's own is `paw.draw.track_colour(track)`
  fill              how opaque the area under the line is, 0 to 1 (0.16); false for none
  width             the line's width in pixels (1.5)
  top, bottom       pixels kept clear above 1 and below 0 (2 each)
  grid              bars (and beats, when `beats`) as lines, true by default
  beats             beat lines too (when beats are at least two cells apart, by default)
  guides            faint lines at a quarter, half and three quarters (true)
  markers           a small mark at each point (true)
  background        a colour to fill the strip with first (none: the cells show)
  ```

  Returns `x(beat)` and `y(value)`, where in the strip a beat and a value are.
- `paw.plot.curve_cells(buf, opts)`: `M.curve` in cells: a connected line of sextants (`paw.opt.curve_glyphs`).
- `paw.plot.lines(w, from, ppb, cell_w)`: The bar and beat lines of a plot `w` pixels wide from the beat `from` at `ppb` pixels a beat: `{ beat, x, bar }` each (`bar` the bar's number for a bar), `x` in pixels from the left, and where the drawing may be cut for each bar, `cut`, the nearest edge of a cell of `cell_w` pixels.
- `paw.plot.span(px, step)`: The stretch of a strip worth drawing, in pixels from its left: what shows of it (`px.view`, all of it when it all shows) and a piece's width either side, in whole stretches of `step` pixels from the strip's left edge, so that a stretch drawn is the same however far the strip is scrolled. Returns the first and last pixel.
- `paw.plot.wave(g, px, opts)`: A waveform in a strip: for each pixel across, the lowest to the highest sample around the middle, its RMS as a brighter band inside that, and a column that reaches full scale in the clip colour. `opts`:

  ```lua
  peaks       `peaks(n)`: `n` `{ min, max, rms }` (-1 to 1) across the
              whole strip, as `api.clip_peaks` gives them; `n` is the
              strip's width in pixels, at most 65536
  color       the wave's colour (the theme's `dim`)
  rms         the RMS band's colour (the wave's, brighter); false for none
  clipped     the colour of a column at full scale (the theme's `red`)
  ```

  Heights follow `paw.opt.wave_scale`, as the cells do.
- `paw.plot.wave_cells(buf, opts)`: `M.wave` in cells: each column from its lowest to its highest sample in eighth blocks (`paw.draw.waveform`), a column at full scale in red. `opts.peaks(n)` is asked for one a column.

## Module paw.plugins

- `paw.plugins.add_dir(dir, name)`: Look for CLAP and VST3 plugins in `dir` as well as where plugins are installed, for the rest of the session, and register those in it now; devices of theirs that a project already holds and that were missing are made. They are listed as coming from `name` (by default the extension whose directory `dir` is in, else `dir`). Works with `--no-plugins` too. Returns `{ kinds, notes }`: the device kinds found and what could not be used; nil where plugins cannot be looked for.

  ```lua
  paw.plugins.add_dir(here .. "/result/lib/clap")   -- `here`: the extension's directory
  ```
- `paw.plugins.key_names(track)`: The key names of a track's devices together; where two name a key, the first in the chain wins.
- `paw.plugins.note_names(device)`: What a device calls its keys, by pitch: a plugin that implements CLAP's `note-name` (a drum kit's drums, a sampler's keyswitches). Empty for the rest. Asked again after `M.names_ttl`.

## Module paw.qf

- `paw.qf.cdo(line, opts)`: Run a command line on each entry of a stack's current list (`:cdo`), the cursor put on the entry first and its address passed as `ctx.target` (and the whole location as `ctx.location`), all as one undo step. With `per_track`, once for each track the entries are on (`:cfdo`). Returns how many times it ran.
- `paw.qf.changed(source)`: Say that a source's entries may have changed.
- `paw.qf.close(loc)`: Close the windows of the tab that show the quickfix list (`loc`: the current window's location list). Returns whether one closed.
- `paw.qf.count(list)`: How many entries of each level a list has: `{ error, warning, info, hint, total }`.
- `paw.qf.current(stack)`: The current list of a stack (the quickfix lists by default), or nil.
- `paw.qf.diagnostics(opts)`: Put diagnostics in a list, as `vim.diagnostic.setqflist`: `opts` has `target` and `severity` (as `paw.diagnostic.get` takes them), `title` ("Diagnostics"), `win` for a location list, `open` to open its window.
- `paw.qf.entry(e, source)`: An entry as the list keeps it: `{ address, location, text, level, severity, source, fix, data }`.
- `paw.qf.fed(source)`: What a source has in the Problems list now.
- `paw.qf.feed(source, entries)`: What a source says now, in the Problems list: its entries there are replaced by these (none takes them out). Any extension may feed it.

  ```lua
  paw.qf.feed("tuning", { { address = "paw://clip/4", text = "out of tune", level = "warning" } })
  ```
- `paw.qf.first(stack)`: Go to the list's first entry, or its last.
- `paw.qf.fix(entries, opts)`: Carry out the fixes of entries (every one of a stack's current list that has one, or those given) as one undo step. Returns how many.
- `paw.qf.fix_title(e)`: The title of an entry's fix, or nil.
- `paw.qf.format(e, list)`: An entry in one line, as said when going to it: `(2 of 7) error: …`.
- `paw.qf.from_diagnostics(target, filter)`: Diagnostics as entries (as `paw.diagnostic.get` takes `target` and `filter`).
- `paw.qf.go(e)`: Put the cursor on an entry's address, in the view that shows it best (focused): a note in the piano roll, a device or parameter in the device panel, a clip, track, lane or stretch of time in the arrange view. Returns whether there was somewhere to go.
- `paw.qf.jump(n, stack)`: Make entry `n` of a stack's current list the current entry and go to it.
- `paw.qf.last(stack)`: Go to the list's last entry.
- `paw.qf.loc_stack(win, make)`: A window's location lists (the current window's without `win`), made when asked for with `make`. A window showing a location list uses the one it shows, as in Neovim.
- `paw.qf.newer(count, stack)`: Go to a newer list in the history (`count` on).
- `paw.qf.older(count, stack)`: Go to an older list in the history (`count` back), or a newer one.
- `paw.qf.open(opts)`: Open the list's window and give it the keyboard: the quickfix list's along the bottom of the tab, the whole width (`opts.height` rows, or `paw.opt.qf_height`); a location list's below its window (`opts.loc`, with `opts.win` the window, the current one by default). A window of the tab that shows it already is gone to. Returns the window.
- `paw.qf.refresh()`: Read every source of the Problems list again.
- `paw.qf.set(entries, opts)`: Put a list of entries in the quickfix lists (a window's location lists with `opts.win`, the current window's with `opts.win = true`), titled `opts.title`, and make it current. A list of the same title already in the history is replaced where it is, with the entry it was on kept; `opts.current = false` leaves another list current. Returns the list.

  ```lua
  paw.qf.set({ { address = "paw://track/3", text = "too quiet", level = "warning" } }, { title = "Levels" })
  ```
- `paw.qf.severity_of(level)`: A severity from 1 (error) to 4 (hint) from a number or a word; nil for none.
- `paw.qf.source(source, fn)`: A source asked for its entries when they may have changed: `fn()` returns them, and is called again after `paw.qf.changed(source)`, once, when the list is next looked at.
- `paw.qf.stack()`: The quickfix lists.
- `paw.qf.status()`: The status line's piece while the quickfix list has entries: `qf 2/7 E2 W5`, the position once one has been gone to. Nil when it is empty.
- `paw.qf.step(count, stack)`: Go `count` entries on (back, when negative) from the current one; the first `]q` goes to the first entry. Stops at the ends, as Neovim does.
- `paw.qf.where(e)`: Where an entry is about, in a few words: `Bass 3.1.00`, `Lead › Synth`, `mix.wav`; empty without an address.

## Module paw.query

- `paw.query.articulations(node)`: A note's articulations: its attribute's (`paw.attr`: the tag, the name and the code, so `pz`, `pizzicato` and `11.A` all find a pizzicato), those the score marks (`meta.notation.art`, a set) and any named in `meta.articulation` (a name or a list of them).
- `paw.query.describe(node)`: A node in a few words, for the quickfix list: `C5 vel 100 at 5.1.00 · Violins pizz`.
- `paw.query.entries(nodes)`: The nodes as quickfix entries.
- `paw.query.field(kind, name, get)`: Add a field to a kind of node: `get(node)` returns its value (a number, text, a boolean, or a list of texts any of which may match).

  ```lua
  paw.query.field("note", "channel", function(node) return node.data.meta.channel end)
  ```
- `paw.query.get(node, name)`: A node's field, or nil.
- `paw.query.location(node)`: A node's location, as the quickfix list and `paw.qf.go` take them.
- `paw.query.parse(q)`: Read a query (text or the table form) once, to run it often. Raises an error that says what is wrong with it.
- `paw.query.run(q)`: Every node a query finds, in the order of the tree (each query of a list of them in turn, none twice).

  ```lua
  for _, n in ipairs(paw.query("note[pitch>=c6]")) do print(n.data.pitch) end
  ```
- `paw.query.select(q, opts)`: Choose what a query finds, where it can be chosen: its clips in the arrange view, its notes in the piano roll (those of each clip); and put everything found in the quickfix list (the window's location list with `opts.loc`). Returns the nodes.

## Module paw.recent

- `paw.recent.clear()`: Forget them all.
- `paw.recent.list()`: The projects opened or saved last, newest first: `{ path, name, time }` (`time` is when, in seconds since 1970). A file that is gone is left out.
- `paw.recent.menu()`: What the window's menu shows: `{ label, path }` each.
- `paw.recent.open(which)`: Open a project from the list, by its place in it or its path; says so when it will not open. Returns whether it did.
- `paw.recent.reopen_last()`: At the start, with no project named: open the newest one when `paw.opt.reopen_last` asks for it. A project that will not open is a message, not the end of the program.
- `paw.recent.use(file)`: Keep the list in `file` and remember projects whatever the program was started with, for tests; `use()` puts things back as they were.

## Module paw.reconnect

- `paw.reconnect.reconnect()`: Try to open the device that went away again. Returns whether it is open.

## Module paw.regex

- `paw.regex.compile(text, opts)`: Make an expression ready to match. Raises an error that says what is wrong with it. `opts.case` true matches case, false ignores it; by default lower case ignores it.
- `paw.regex.try(text, opts)`: An expression ready to match, or nil and what is wrong with it.

## Module paw.remote

- `paw.remote.closed(client)`: A connection closed: nothing more is sent to it.
- `paw.remote.listeners()`: Who is listening: { client = { patterns = {...}, watching = bool }, ... }.
- `paw.remote.push(client)`: Send a connection what has changed of the frontend's state since it was last sent anything: nothing at all when nothing has.

## Module paw.roles

- `paw.roles.begin(name, win)`: A view is about to be drawn on the terminal's screen (`win`, the id of its window, if any): its hit regions start afresh.
- `paw.roles.define(name, spec)`: Define a role: `spec.cells(buf, props, ctx)` draws it in cells (it is required: the terminal comes first); `spec.props` names its props and what they hold, for documentation and `paw.ui.roles`; `spec.bound` the props a frontend takes from the live value instead when the mark is bound to one, which are not sent to it.
- `paw.roles.finish()`: The view being drawn is done: what it marks after is no hit region.
- `paw.roles.gesture(view, e)`: An event on a hit region (`e.hit`, `e.rect`) to its view: true when it was taken.
- `paw.roles.hit(buf, x, y, w, h, action)`: `buf:hit(x, y, w, h, action)`: see the top of this file.
- `paw.roles.input(client, id, view, win, event, held)`: A pointer event from a frontend that is sent scenes (paw/scene.lua), in units of its window `id`, over the view `view` (its window of the layout `win`, if any): on a hit region of the scene it was sent, to the region's gesture, with `x` and `y` in units; a drag begun there goes on in units (`held`, what the frontend's watcher keeps). True when taken.
- `paw.roles.mark(buf, role, x, y, w, h, props)`: `buf:mark(role, x, y, w, h, props)`: see the top of this file.
- `paw.roles.pointer(view, name, event)`: A mouse event in the terminal, in the cells of the view it is over (as its `on_mouse` takes it, with `view_x`, `view_y`, `win`): to the gesture of the hit region under it. True when it was taken.

## Module paw.roll_clips

- `paw.roll_clips.activate(id)`: Make a clip the active one. One that is not editable yet takes the old active clip's place in the set; the cursor stays where it is in the song.
- `paw.roll_clips.active()`: The id of the active clip, or nil with no clip open.
- `paw.roll_clips.context()`: The context notes: those of the shown tracks' clips (not the editable ones) that sound within the editable clips' stretch, in the roll's beats: `{ pitch, start, length, velocity, clip, track, color }` each, at most `paw.opt.roll_context_max` of them. Kept until the project, the set of clips or the toggles change.
- `paw.roll_clips.context_at(pitch, beat)`: The context note on `pitch` sounding at roll beat `beat`, if any.
- `paw.roll_clips.cycle(n)`: Make the clip `n` places after the active one (before it, with a negative `n`) active, the editable clips taken in the order they start.
- `paw.roll_clips.editable(id)`: Whether a clip is one of the editable ones.
- `paw.roll_clips.ids()`: The ids of the editable clips, the active one first, then the others in the order they were added.
- `paw.roll_clips.note_at(pitch, beat, parts)`: The note of an editable clip on `pitch` sounding at roll beat `beat`, the active clip's first: the note (in the roll's beats), its place and its part.
- `paw.roll_clips.notes(range, parts)`: The notes of the editable clips in the roll's beats, in the order they start (lower pitches first in a chord), each with `clip` (its clip's id), `place` (its place among that clip's notes, for `edit_notes`) and `offset`. With one clip they are that clip's notes in its own order. `range` is as for `Clip:notes`, its beats the roll's.
- `paw.roll_clips.offset(id)`: Where a clip's beats are in the roll: add this to them.
